findings.topic: Reading Apple HealthKit from a Flutter iOS app (late 2026)

claims.claim: Main maintained package is pub.dev 'health' v13.3.2, now published by carp.dk (repo moved to carp-dk/carp-health-flutter). It exposes 111 HealthDataType values. Present: STEPS, ACTIVE_ENERGY_BURNED, BASAL_ENERGY_BURNED, WORKOUT (+WORKOUT_ROUTE), SLEEP_* stages (ASLEEP, AWAKE, AWAKE_IN_BED, IN_BED, OUT_OF_BED, DEEP, LIGHT, REM, UNKNOWN, SESSION), WEIGHT, BODY_FAT_PERCENTAGE, LEAN_BODY_MASS, BODY_MASS_INDEX, HEIGHT, RESTING_HEART_RATE, HEART_RATE, HRV SDNN and RMSSD, EXERCISE_TIME, APPLE_STAND_TIME, APPLE_STAND_HOUR, APPLE_MOVE_TIME, MINDFULNESS, WATER, DIETARY_ENERGY_CONSUMED (+ many dietary macros/micros, NUTRITION), DISTANCE_WALKING_RUNNING, FLIGHTS_CLIMBED.
claims.design_implication: Covers nearly all required metrics out of the box, with the two gaps below. Workouts carry type/duration/distance/energy; heart rate per workout must be fetched as a separate HEART_RATE query over the workout window (not verified that the package attaches it).

claims.claim: The 'health' package has NO VO2MAX and NO TOOTHBRUSHING enum value (verified against the 111-value enum list). Both exist in HealthKit itself (vo2Max quantity type; toothbrushingEvent category type).
claims.design_implication: Reading VO2max and toothbrushing events requires a small native Swift shim (MethodChannel) or a fork/PR of the plugin. Alternative for toothbrushing: just make it an in-app manual/Watch-complication check-in and treat HealthKit as optional bonus. Brushing events from Apple Watch only exist when the user brushes with a connected Bluetooth/Watch-detected brush flow, so manual tap is the realistic baseline.

claims.claim: The released 'health' package does not support HKObserverQuery / enableBackgroundDelivery on iOS (README never mentions it; only Android Health Connect background-read permission). A PR #521 (carp-health-flutter) adds registerBackgroundDeliveryCallback + configureBackgroundDelivery using three native iOS files (HKObserverManager, HKBackgroundDeliveryWorker running a headless FlutterEngine, HKDeliveryUserDefaults). It is OPEN, unreviewed, not merged, no device validation reported, and the engine crashes if run in foreground.
claims.design_implication: Do not depend on an unmerged PR. Background delivery needs native code. Using the 'health' package for foreground reads plus your own small shim for background wake-ups is the lowest-risk split.

claims.claim: Alternative package health_connector v3.14.0 (verified publisher, MIT, iOS+Android, 150+ types claimed, aggregateSum/Avg/Min/Max, incremental synchronize() with sync tokens). Maintainer explicitly declined to add HKObserverQuery background delivery (Sep 2026) and suggests the workmanager plugin plus synchronize(). VO2max and toothbrushing support not confirmed on the package page (a type catalog exists but was not fetched). Low adoption (~1.9k downloads).
claims.design_implication: Worth a look for its aggregation and anchored-style sync, but workmanager on iOS maps to BGTaskScheduler, which is opportunistic and not data-triggered. It is a weaker background mechanism than HKObserverQuery for this use case.

claims.claim: Native background pattern (Swift): create HKObserverQuery per type, call healthStore.enableBackgroundDelivery(for:frequency:) (.immediate/.hourly/.daily), and on wake query samples since last sync, upload, then call completionHandler on EVERY code path including errors. If the handler is not called, the system stops delivering. Requires the HealthKit background-delivery entitlement and registering observers in application(_:didFinishLaunching) so a cold relaunch re-arms them. Use a background URLSession for the upload, and send sample UUIDs as idempotency keys.
claims.design_implication: The shim is small: roughly 100-200 lines of Swift in AppDelegate (observers for steps, workouts, sleep, body mass, etc.; an HKAnchoredObjectQuery with persisted anchor per type; background URLSession POST of JSON to the server). It can bypass Dart entirely, which avoids the headless-engine fragility. Estimate is my inference, not a sourced figure.

claims.claim: Background delivery reliability caveat: Apple Developer Forums report HKObserverQuery with background delivery on watchOS 26 stops delivering after a day or two even with the handler fixed. Apple DTS confirmed it as a known issue; feedback FB20344425 was closed as 'works as designed' and FB20692241 refiled. This thread is about watchOS-side apps; iPhone-side behaviour was not tested in the source. Other forum threads report variable frequency across devices.
claims.design_implication: Never rely on background delivery alone. Always also sync on app foreground/launch, on a BGAppRefreshTask, and have the server detect gaps. Daily sync is easy to satisfy with open-app catch-up plus best-effort background pushes.

claims.claim: HealthKit read permissions are privacy-opaque: requestAuthorization success means the sheet was processed, not that read was granted. Denied or revoked read types simply return empty results indistinguishable from no data. Only write (share) status is queryable via authorizationStatus. Also the device must be unlocked to request data (plugin README) and protected health data is not readable while the phone is locked, which affects background wake-ups.
claims.design_implication: Build an in-app 'data collection checklist' where the user confirms each source (Watch worn, Renpho synced to Health) and detect staleness server-side (no steps for 48h means prompt them to check Settings > Health > Data Access). Request all read types in a single sheet at onboarding. Note the Apple doc fetch returned only a title, so the doc wording is from general knowledge, though the behaviour is long-established.

claims.claim: watchOS 26 / iOS 26 Sleep Score: no public HealthKit type or developer API for the score was found. A developer forum post says none exists. Apple's score (0-100: duration 50, bedtime consistency 30, interruptions 20; stages not used) is computed in the Health app from sleep analysis data and also works with third-party sleep data. I could not retrieve Apple's iOS 26 HealthKit release notes to be sure.
claims.design_implication: Compute your own sleep score server-side from raw sleep-stage samples, using the published weighting (duration, bedtime consistency, interruptions) as a template. This also keeps scoring consistent and fair across both users. Re-verify against Apple HealthKit docs before building.

claims.claim: Dedup and source pitfalls: HealthKit merges iPhone, Watch, and third-party samples; one type can have multiple sources. The 'health' package offers removeDuplicates and, on iOS, a recording-method filter that only distinguishes automatic vs manual. Sample UUIDs should be used as idempotency keys. Sleep stage SLEEP_ASLEEP maps to asleepUnspecified and SLEEP_LIGHT maps to asleepCore on iOS. Overlapping sleep from Watch and iPhone or other apps needs merging.
claims.design_implication: Store raw samples with source bundle ID/device name, sample UUID, start/end ISO timestamps with UTC offset. Do dedup/priority server-side (e.g. Watch over iPhone for steps/HR/sleep, Renpho source for body mass) or use HKStatisticsCollectionQuery for steps/energy, which applies HealthKit's own source-priority merging. Plain sample sums of steps can double count iPhone+Watch. Timezone handling is my inference: store the user's local-day boundary at sample time rather than deriving it from the server timezone.

claims.claim: Renpho scale data reaches HealthKit only if the Renpho app has Apple Health sync enabled; the data then shows as body mass, body fat %, lean body mass, BMI samples with Renpho as source. This is inferred and not verified from a source in this research.
claims.design_implication: Add a checklist step to verify Renpho > Apple Health toggle, and consume weight, body fat, and lean mass via the health package (all available types).

findings.recommended_approach: Hybrid: Flutter app using pub.dev 'health' (v13.3.2) for onboarding permission request and foreground/on-launch reads of almost everything (steps, workouts, sleep stages, weight/body fat/lean mass/BMI, resting HR, HRV, active energy, exercise time, stand, mindful, water, dietary energy). Add a small native Swift shim (MethodChannel plus AppDelegate, roughly 100-200 lines, my estimate) that (a) reads the two missing types, vo2Max and toothbrushingEvent, and (b) registers HKObserverQuery plus enableBackgroundDelivery for a handful of types (workouts, sleep, body mass, steps) using HKAnchoredObjectQuery with persisted anchors and a background URLSession upload straight to the Go/Postgres server, with completionHandler on every path. Treat background delivery as best-effort: also sync on every app foreground, schedule a BGAppRefreshTask, and have the server flag gaps. Send raw samples with UUID, source bundle ID, start/end plus UTC offset; dedupe and apply source priority (Watch over iPhone, Renpho for body composition) server-side and use HKStatisticsCollectionQuery for daily steps/energy totals. Compute your own sleep score server-side from sleep stages. Make toothbrushing a manual in-app tap with HealthKit as optional bonus. Test everything on physical devices.
alternatives: Wait for or contribute to carp-health-flutter PR #521 for background delivery - open, unreviewed, headless-engine design, so risky as a dependency; a vendored fork is possible.

Use health_connector (v3.14.0) with its synchronize() incremental tokens and workmanager - cross-platform and typed, but background wakeups are opportunistic via BGTaskScheduler rather than data-driven, and VO2max/toothbrushing coverage is unverified.
Fully native Swift sync helper (the shim grown to cover all types), with Flutter handling only the UI - most reliable on background delivery, more Swift to maintain.
Apple Shortcuts/Health Auto Export-style automation pushing to the server - zero native code but depends on third-party apps and automation triggers; not verified in this research.
Open Wearables iOS SDK (mentioned in the cited article, native Swift) - not evaluated.
cannot_do: Cannot read the native Apple Sleep Score from HealthKit - no public API found.
Cannot detect whether the user denied read permission - HealthKit returns empty results by design.

Cannot guarantee background sync with the app terminated or the phone locked - protected data is unavailable while locked, and background delivery is best-effort with known watchOS 26 reliability issues.
Cannot read VO2max or toothbrushing events with the 'health' package as-is.
Cannot verify iPhone-side HKObserverQuery stability on iOS 26 from sources - only watchOS-side reports were found; it needs a physical device test.
Cannot test HealthKit in the iOS Simulator with real Watch/Renpho data - physical devices are needed.
open_questions_for_user: Is a ~100-200 line Swift shim acceptable for the background sync plus VO2max/toothbrushing, given 'not Swift-only' means Flutter UI is fine?
Is real-time sync required, or is 'by next morning, plus whenever the app is opened' enough? That decides how much to invest in background delivery.
Does the Renpho app already sync to Apple Health on both phones, and do both have Apple Watches worn to sleep (needed for sleep stages and HRV)?
Is toothbrushing tracked via Apple Watch auto-detect or only manual taps? Auto-detect requires a connected toothbrush app or Watch brushing detection; confirm what you actually own.
Should the scoring apply a handicap for Nadia's work day, and which source (Watch vs iPhone) wins for conflicting steps?

verdicts.claim: 1. health v13.3.2 by carp.dk, 111 types, listed types present
verdicts.evidence: pub.dev/packages/health shows 13.3.2, verified publisher carp.dk, repo github.com/carp-dk/carp-health-flutter, Android+iOS, published about 2 months ago. The enum page (pub.dev/documentation/health/latest/health/HealthDataType.html) lists 111 values including WORKOUT_ROUTE, both HRV types, APPLE_STAND_HOUR, APPLE_MOVE_TIME, APPLE_STAND_TIME, MINDFULNESS, WATER, NUTRITION, DISTANCE_WALKING_RUNNING and FLIGHTS_CLIMBED.
verdicts.correction: Sleep values are prefixed: SLEEP_ASLEEP, SLEEP_AWAKE, SLEEP_AWAKE_IN_BED, SLEEP_IN_BED, SLEEP_OUT_OF_BED, SLEEP_DEEP, SLEEP_LIGHT, SLEEP_REM, SLEEP_UNKNOWN, SLEEP_SESSION. Not a substantive error.

verdicts.claim: 2. health has no VO2MAX or TOOTHBRUSHING; both exist in HealthKit
verdicts.evidence: The 111-value enum has neither. Apple documents vo2Max as a quantity type (developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit/hkquantitytypeidentifier/vo2max), saved automatically on Watch Series 3 or later, units ml/kg/min. toothbrushingEvent is not on the pages I fetched; I rely on prior knowledge that it exists (HKCategoryTypeIdentifier, iOS 13+).
verdicts.correction: Toothbrushing existence is not verified from a fetched primary source, so treat that half as likely but unchecked. The 'no VO2MAX' half is solid.

verdicts.claim: 3. Released health lacks iOS HKObserverQuery background delivery; PR #521 adds it but is open, unreviewed, unvalidated, crashes in foreground
verdicts.evidence: github.com/carp-dk/carp-health-flutter/pull/521 'iOS: HealthKit background delivery': open, opened Sep 10 2026, force-push Sep 26, comment Oct 21 2026, no reviews, no labels or milestone. Adds registerBackgroundDeliveryCallback and configureBackgroundDelivery with HKObserverManager, HKBackgroundDeliveryWorker (headless FlutterEngine) and HKDeliveryUserDefaults. Engine crashes in foreground so it runs only when backgrounded. The author reports only a successful iOS build and flutter analyze, no device testing. pub.dev README has no iOS background section.
verdicts.correction: Add that the PR author links an earlier design to a production engine abort and an earlier per-type-engine version was killed by the watchdog; it is only build-verified. Its Dart-callback-in-headless-engine approach is unproven on devices.

verdicts.claim: 4. health_connector v3.14.0, MIT, maintainer declined observer background delivery, suggests workmanager + synchronize(), VO2/toothbrushing unconfirmed, low adoption
verdicts.evidence: pub.dev/packages/health_connector: 3.14.0, verified publisher phamtunglam.com, MIT, Android+iOS, 1.93k downloads. Issue #227 (github.com/fam-tung-lam/health_connector/issues/227): opened Sep 15 2026, maintainer replied Sep 16 'not planning to add this feature in the near future', recommends synchronize plus workmanager via an incremental-background-data-sync recipe, would reconsider on concrete limitations. Issue still open.
verdicts.correction: The page says 143 typed data types, not 150+ (the 150+ is the package's own marketing blurb in search snippets). VO2 max and toothbrushing still unconfirmed because the type catalog was not retrieved.

verdicts.claim: 5. Native background pattern: HKObserverQuery, enableBackgroundDelivery, completionHandler on every path, entitlement, register at launch, background URLSession, UUID idempotency
verdicts.evidence: developer.apple.com/forums/thread/801627: DTS and community state the completion handler must be called on every path including errors, and after async work finishes; otherwise the system stops delivering. The entitlement, launch-time registration, background URLSession and UUID idempotency points come from my background knowledge and the cited openwearables article, which I did not re-fetch.
verdicts.correction: Add that async work must have a timeout so the handler is always eventually called. Note that the HealthKit background-delivery entitlement is required on iOS (com.apple.developer.healthkit.background-delivery).

verdicts.claim: 6. Background delivery stops after a day or two on watchOS 26; DTS confirmed known issue; FB20344425 closed works as designed; FB20692241 refiled
verdicts.evidence: Thread 801627: OP on Apple Watch Series 8/10, watchOS 26.1, says delivery of heart rate and active energy stops, restart restores it temporarily, recurs within 2-3 days. DTS (Sep 2025) said it is a reported issue and to file feedback; in Oct 2025 DTS said a missed completion handler on error is 'as designed' and the OP's corrected snippet 'looks good'. OP reports FB20344425 status 'Investigation complete - Works as currently designed' and filed FB20692241 with the corrected code. I did not fetch thread 814914.
verdicts.correction: DTS did not clearly confirm a platform bug; the 'as designed' response was about the missing-handler case, and the corrected-code case is still tracked in FB20692241 with no stated root cause. It is watchOS-hosted, 2-3 days not 'a day or two', and iPhone-side behavior is untested. Treat as 'unresolved reports of unreliable delivery', not 'confirmed known issue'. Thread 814914 claim unverified.

verdicts.claim: 7. Read permissions are privacy-opaque; success only means the sheet was processed; only share status is queryable; device must be unlocked / protected data unreadable while locked
verdicts.evidence: The Apple doc page body did not load via fetch (only the title), so the first two points are from well-established API behavior (read denial is indistinguishable from no data; authorizationStatus is share-only) rather than a fetched quote. Apple documents that protected health data is unavailable while the device is locked (HealthKit data protection); the README unlock note was not re-verified.
verdicts.correction: Add that the background-delivery wake while the phone is locked can fire but protected sample queries may fail or return nothing until first unlock, so anchored queries must not advance the anchor on error.

verdicts.claim: 8. No public Sleep Score API in HealthKit; score computed in Health app (duration 50, bedtime consistency 30, interruptions 20)
verdicts.evidence: I did not re-fetch the cited forum tag page, Macworld or 9to5Mac articles, and did not find Apple iOS 26 HealthKit release notes. No contrary evidence turned up.
verdicts.correction: Keep as medium-confidence: no public sleep score type found as of this check; verify against Apple's iOS 26 HealthKit release notes before relying on the absence. Computing your own score server-side is a safe plan either way.

verification.revised_recommendation: The hybrid recommendation stands with three adjustments. (1) Use health 13.3.2 for permissions and foreground reads. It is current and maintained. (2) Do not wait on or depend on PR #521. It is open, unreviewed and only build-verified. If you want background delivery without writing native code, you could vendor that branch behind a flag, but the Swift shim with HKObserverQuery, HKAnchoredObjectQuery, a background URLSession and the completion handler on every path (with a timeout) is the lower-risk choice. The shim also covers the two missing types, vo2Max and toothbrushingEvent. Verify toothbrushingEvent against Apple's docs when writing it. (3) Treat background delivery as best effort. Reports of it silently stopping exist (watchOS 26, 2-3 days, FB20692241 unresolved), so keep the sync on foreground, BGAppRefreshTask, and server-side gap flags. Never advance the anchor when a query fails (for example when the device is locked). Keep the manual toothbrushing tap as the primary source. health_connector is not a better option: it has the same lack of iOS observer support, 143 types rather than 150+, and low adoption. Sleep score: compute your own server-side. Re-check Apple's iOS 26 release notes for a public score API before finalizing.

findings.topic: Getting body-composition data out of a Renpho smart scale (Apple Health sync, cloud/BLE alternatives, two-user handling)

claims.claim: Renpho Health app (blue icon) syncs to Apple Health: Body Fat Percentage, Body Mass Index and Lean Body Mass are explicitly named in the App Store text; weight is described as synced to HealthKit too. Likely HK types: bodyMass, bodyFatPercentage, bodyMassIndex, leanBodyMass (type names are inferred from Apple's standard identifiers, not stated by Renpho).
claims.design_implication: Treat HealthKit as guaranteeing only weight, BMI, body fat % and lean mass. Build trends and head-to-head body-comp scoring on those four and nothing else.

claims.claim: Muscle mass, bone mass, body water %, visceral fat, BMR and metabolic/body age are reported to stay inside the Renpho app only (secondary source says Apple Health lacks matching fields; the App Store text also mentions resting-calorie data and height, unverified). Not independently confirmed per-type.
claims.design_implication: Do not depend on visceral fat, water or muscle mass from HealthKit. If wanted, they need the cloud API or BLE path. Verify empirically by querying HealthKit on a real device after one weigh-in.

claims.claim: Apple Health sync from the Renpho app is phone-mediated: most Renpho models are Bluetooth, so data reaches HealthKit only when the Renpho app receives the reading (phone near scale, app able to connect). Some reviewers report flaky Apple Health sync. Each partner's HealthKit exists only on their own phone, which is correct for a two-user app.
claims.design_implication: The Flutter app should read HealthKit on each phone and upload to the Go backend, with a visible 'last weigh-in synced' timestamp and a manual weight entry fallback.

claims.claim: No official public Renpho API. The App Store listing mentions shareable reports but I could not verify an official CSV export; one low-quality German how-to site claims a CSV export exists in the Health app.
claims.design_implication: Do not plan on a CSV import pipeline. Check the in-app settings once on a real device; if present it is only useful for a one-time historical backfill.

claims.claim: Unofficial cloud clients exist. Legacy Renpho-app API projects (antoinebou12/hass_renpho, neilzilla/hass-renpho) are reported broken or stale for newer accounts. StartupBros-com/hass-renpho-health targets the Renpho Health API at cloud.renpho.com, exposing weight, BMI, body fat, muscle mass, water, bone mass, visceral fat, BMR, body age, protein, subcutaneous fat, skeletal muscle; it uses reverse-engineered AES-128-ECB, polls 5 min minimum, and logs in with the user's app credentials. teknikqa/ha-renpho is similar and only tested on one live account. Wire protocol credited to forkerer/RenphoGarminSync-CLI and danvaneijck/renpho-api.
claims.design_implication: A Go backend poller using each partner's Renpho credentials is the only way to get the full panel (visceral fat, water, muscle etc.) without BLE. It is fragile: undocumented API, can break on any app update, and may log the partner out of the app. Use as optional enrichment, not as the primary path. I found no renpho2mqtt project in search.

claims.claim: Renpho multi-user: the app supports multiple profiles. Auto-assignment is weight-based (match weight to each profile's history), per third-party description only; no official doc found. Failure reports: a couple sharing one account saw duplicated stats, and a reviewer had a partner's weight land on their profile and the bad point lingered until superseded.
claims.design_implication: Give Nick and Nadia separate Renpho accounts/profiles on their own phones. If their weights are far apart, mis-assignment risk is low. Add backend sanity checks (reject a weigh-in more than a few percent or ~2 kg away from that person's recent value, prompt to confirm) and an 'it was not me' discard button.

claims.claim: Direct BLE: most common Renpho family is the QN-Scale protocol (service 0xFFF0 style). Confirmed-working in the unofficial Python client: ES-CS20M (some revisions), ES-26M, ES-28ML, ES-30M, ES-32MD, R-MSB01. Experimental: ES-26BB-B, R-A012, R-A016, some ES-CS20M revisions on 0x55aa (GATT) or 0xaabb (broadcast, weight only). Newer ES-CS20M revisions (HVIN ESCS20MB2) use Renpho's own protocol on service 0x1A10. Marketed model name is unreliable; the HVIN sticker revision suffix determines protocol.
claims.design_implication: Before committing to BLE, read the HVIN on the underside of the Renpho scale and match it against these lists. The user said only 'Renpho smart scale' so the model is unknown.

claims.claim: BLE specifics: QN extended flavor will not start a measurement without a profile; the client must write a profile (height, age, sex) within about 2 seconds or the scale returns weight only. Body composition is derived from raw impedance using approximate algorithms (only 0x03 and 0x04 approximated in software), so values will not match the Renpho app exactly. Broadcast-only units give weight only (body comp estimated from BMI). Reading stored offline records can delete them from the scale and hide them from the official app. The Python client was only tested on macOS. openScale (Android) is the main open-source reference for QN handling but it is Android-only.
claims.design_implication: BLE-direct from Flutter (flutter_blue_plus / CoreBluetooth) is technically feasible but means owning the protocol, formulas and conflict with the Renpho app which also wants the scale. iOS cannot reliably scan in background for a passive weigh-in, so the app must be foregrounded. Worth it only as a stretch goal, with the Renpho app kept for everything else.

claims.claim: I did not verify Flutter-specific BLE libraries, iOS background BLE limits, or HealthKit write semantics from sources in this pass; those statements are from general knowledge.
claims.design_implication: Spike these on a physical iPhone before relying on them.

findings.recommended_approach: Primary path: each partner has their own Renpho Health account and profile on their own iPhone, Renpho writes to Apple Health, and the Flutter app reads HealthKit (weight, body fat %, BMI, lean body mass) via a plugin such as health, then uploads to the Go/Postgres backend tagged with the device owner. This is zero reverse engineering, per-person identity comes free from the phone, and it survives Renpho API changes. Add manual weight entry plus a sanity filter and 'not me' discard for mis-assigned weigh-ins, and a 'last synced' staleness indicator. Score on trends (4 HealthKit fields), not on absolute body-comp numbers, since BIA values are noisy and consumer-grade. Optional enrichment later: a Go poller against cloud.renpho.com using the hass-renpho-health protocol for visceral fat, water and muscle mass, treated as best-effort. Keep BLE-direct as a last resort stretch goal, gated on confirming scale HVIN.
alternatives: Cloud API poller (hass-renpho-health style) in the Go backend: richest metrics, no phone involvement, but undocumented, reverse-engineered, breaks on app updates, uses stored credentials.

Direct BLE from Flutter (QN protocol): independent of Renpho cloud and app, but model-dependent, must supply profile within about 2 s, approximate body-comp formulas, foreground only on iOS, and conflicts with the official app.
Replace or supplement the scale with one that has a documented path (for example a Withings scale with an official API), only if Renpho proves unreliable.
One-time historical backfill via in-app export, if it exists (unverified).
cannot_do: Could not confirm the exact HKQuantityTypeIdentifier list Renpho writes; only Renpho's own text naming body fat %, BMI, lean body mass (plus weight).
Could not verify an official CSV export in the Renpho Health app.
Could not verify Renpho's own documentation on how auto user recognition works or its weight-gap threshold; only third-party descriptions.
Could not identify Nick's scale model/HVIN, so BLE protocol support is unconfirmed.
Found no renpho2mqtt project; did not check Home Assistant's core BLE integration for Renpho support.
Did not verify Flutter BLE plugins or iOS background BLE behavior with sources.
open_questions_for_user: What is the HVIN / model number on the sticker under the Renpho scale, and is it Bluetooth-only or Wi-Fi?
Do you and Nadia each already have a separate Renpho Health account, or share one?
Are your weights far enough apart that the scale's auto-recognition has been right so far?
Do you care about visceral fat, water and muscle mass, or are weight, body fat % and lean mass enough for scoring?
Are you willing to rely on an unofficial reverse-engineered cloud API for optional extra metrics?
Is the Renpho app currently syncing to Apple Health on both phones (check Health > Sources)?

verdicts.claim: 1. Renpho Health syncs weight, body fat %, BMI, lean body mass to Apple Health
verdicts.evidence: App Store listing (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/renpho-health/id1543340610) has two lists. The setup step says Body Fat Percentage, BMI and Lean Body Mass sync. The scale description says weight, body fat %, fat weight, height, BMI and resting calorie consumption sync to HealthKit. scorevitals (https://scorevitals.com/howtos/sync-smart-scale-to-apple-health) lists weight, body fat %, BMI, lean body mass. pub.dev health 13.3.2 (https://pub.dev/packages/health) supports WEIGHT, BODY_FAT_PERCENTAGE, BODY_MASS_INDEX, LEAN_BODY_MASS on iOS and was published about 2 months ago, so it is maintained.
verdicts.correction: Add that the App Store lists two non-identical sets. Weight is only in the scale-description list, not the setup-step list. The listing also mentions fat weight, height and resting calories, which may or may not be written. Verify on a real device by checking Health > Browse > Body Measurements. Do not depend on the extras.

verdicts.claim: 2. Muscle mass, bone mass, body water, visceral fat, BMR and body age stay inside the Renpho app
verdicts.evidence: scorevitals says muscle mass, bone mass and body water stay in the app because Apple Health has no matching fields. It does not mention visceral fat, BMR or body age. The App Store text says resting calorie consumption syncs, so BMR may reach HealthKit as a basal-energy sample. A search found nothing saying bone mass or visceral fat is written.
verdicts.correction: Muscle mass, bone mass and body water stay in-app per a secondary source. Visceral fat is not documented as synced. BMR/resting calories may sync, since the App Store text names resting calorie consumption. Body age is unverified. Confirm per type on the actual device.

verdicts.claim: 3. Apple Health sync is phone-mediated over Bluetooth; each partner's HealthKit is on their own phone
verdicts.evidence: scorevitals says the Renpho app must be open and within range, and that the scale stores up to 20 offline measurements and syncs them on the next app open. The App Store text does not mention Bluetooth.
verdicts.correction: Refine the statement. Readings are not lost when the phone is away. The scale buffers up to 20 and the Renpho app backfills them, so HealthKit samples carry the weigh-in time and may arrive late. The staleness indicator should key on the sample's date, not the sync time. The app must be opened at least occasionally. The flaky-sync reports remain anecdotal.

verdicts.claim: 4. Unofficial cloud clients exist, including StartupBros-com/hass-renpho-health (cloud.renpho.com, AES-128-ECB, 5 min polling minimum)
verdicts.evidence: https://github.com/StartupBros-com/hass-renpho-health: Renpho Health cloud API at cloud.renpho.com, AES-128-ECB, metrics weight, BMI, body fat, muscle mass, water, bone mass, BMR, visceral fat, body age, protein, subcutaneous fat, skeletal muscle. Default poll 1 hour, 5 minute minimum. It is credited as reverse-engineered from RenphoGarminSync-CLI. The repo has 5 commits, 1 star, 0 forks, 2 open issues, so it is very young and low-adoption. I did not check the other repos (hass_renpho, teknikqa/ha-renpho) or the HA community thread.
verdicts.correction: Add that hass-renpho-health is a very young single-maintainer repo (5 commits, 1 star) and that it needs the user's Renpho credentials. Treat it as fragile. The staleness claims about the legacy projects are unverified by me.

verdicts.claim: 5. Renpho supports multiple profiles; auto-assignment is weight-based per third-party sources; failure reports exist
verdicts.evidence: The App Store text confirms the app 'allows the user to create multiple personal profiles to keep your data separated'. I did not fetch the scienceinsights or techadvisor pages, so the weight-matching mechanism and the failure anecdotes are unverified by me.
verdicts.correction: Multiple profiles are confirmed. Weight-based auto-assignment and the misassignment anecdotes are unverified third-party claims. The design still holds, since the recommended path avoids shared-scale assignment ambiguity only if each partner's weigh-in lands on their own profile and phone. With one shared scale, misassignment risk remains, so keep the 'not me' discard and a sanity filter.

verdicts.claim: 6. Direct BLE: QN-Scale is the most common protocol; model support list; newer ES-CS20M revisions use service 0x1A10; HVIN suffix determines protocol
verdicts.evidence: https://github.com/ronnnnnnnnnnnnn/renpho-escs20m lists confirmed-working models ES-CS20M (HVIN ESCS20MA2 or ESCS20MN), ES-26M, ES-28ML, ES-30M, ES-32MD, R-MSB01. Experimental: Arboleaf CS20M, 0xaabb broadcast (weight only), and 0x55aa basic (ES-CS20MB1, ES-26BB-B, R-A012, R-A016) and extended (ESCS20MB2). It says the marketed model name is unreliable and the HVIN revision suffix is the better guide. https://blescalesync.dev/guide/supported-scales calls QN 'the most common protocol' and says newer ES-CS20M revisions use Renpho's own protocol on service 0x1A10.
verdicts.correction: Minor point. In the repo, ESCS20MB2 sits under the 0x55aa extended flavor and the 0x55aa basic flavor streams on vendor service 0x1A10 (notify char 0x2A10). Wording about which revision maps to which flavor is slightly muddled in the claim. blescalesync also lists ES-WBE28 as standard GATT and R-MSC04 as weight-only. I did not verify the openScale pages or issues 1509 and 1523.

verdicts.claim: 7. BLE specifics: profile write within about 2 seconds, approximate body comp, stored-record deletion, macOS-only testing, openScale is Android-only
verdicts.evidence: The renpho-escs20m README confirms a roughly 2 second window after the first stable frame ('to avoid losing body fat to the scale's commit window'), that reading a stored record deletes it from the scale and hides it from other clients including the official app, and 'Tested on macOS (Apple Silicon)', with Linux via bleak unverified. blescalesync notes some ES-CS20M/Elis 1 variants only broadcast with body comp estimated from BMI. The blescalesync supported-scales page does not mention the 0x03/0x04 approximations. I did not verify the 'extended flavor will not start without a profile' wording, the approximation detail, or openScale's Android-only status.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: 2 s window, stored-record deletion, macOS-only testing. Unverified here: the 0x03/0x04 approximation detail, the 'weight only without profile' behavior, and openScale being Android-only. Also note iOS CoreBluetooth background limits were not researched, so BLE-direct on iOS is untested territory.

verification.revised_recommendation: The primary path stands: each partner uses their own Renpho Health account and profile on their own iPhone, Renpho writes to Apple Health, and the Flutter app reads HealthKit through the health plugin (13.3.2, maintained). The plugin supports WEIGHT, BODY_FAT_PERCENTAGE, BODY_MASS_INDEX and LEAN_BODY_MASS on iOS. Three adjustments. First, treat weight and body fat % as the only fields guaranteed to be in HealthKit. The App Store text is inconsistent about the rest, so verify on a real device before building scoring on BMI or lean mass. Second, base the staleness indicator on the sample timestamp, since the scale buffers up to 20 offline readings and the Renpho app backfills them with the original time. Both partners must also open the Renpho app now and then. Third, keep the 'not me' discard and sanity filter, because profile auto-assignment on a shared scale is unverified third-party lore. Keep the cloud poller (hass-renpho-health protocol) as an optional best-effort enrichment for visceral fat, water and muscle mass. It is a 5-commit, 1-star reverse-engineered project that needs each partner's Renpho credentials. Keep BLE-direct as a last resort, gated on the HVIN sticker. It is only validated on macOS, reading stored records erases them from the official app, and iOS behavior is untested."

findings.topic: Measuring iPhone screen time for a TestFlight-distributed gamified habit app (Flutter host, native Swift extensions)

claims.claim: A DeviceActivityReport extension is intentionally sandboxed so its usage data cannot be exported to the host app. An Apple DTS engineer answered 'Yes' to 'Is DeviceActivityReportExtension intentionally sandboxed so Screen Time data cannot be exported to the containing app?' and pointed to forum thread 817516 (not fetched by me).
claims.design_implication: Do not plan on App Group, UserDefaults, file, or network export from the report extension. Reports can only render usage inside Apple's own view hosted in your app. Secondary sources report writes silently no-op.

claims.claim: A DeviceActivityReport view can display accurate totals to the user inside the host app (via DeviceActivityReport SwiftUI view), but the host app never sees the numbers. Reports say the report extension also fails to launch on some builds (iOS 26.4 thread).
claims.design_implication: Report can serve as a read-only personal dashboard (Flutter UiKitView/platform view embedding a SwiftUI DeviceActivityReport), but it cannot feed points, streaks, or the server. The extension has reliability issues on recent iOS.

claims.claim: DeviceActivityMonitor extension can write to an App Group and is the commonly used workaround. A repeating daily schedule (00:00-23:59:59) with DeviceActivityEvents at thresholds fires eventDidReachThreshold; the extension records the hit in App Group UserDefaults and the host app reads it. Crunchybagel describes this pattern used in Streaks (mark day missed). Extension memory limit about 5 MB.
claims.design_implication: Coarse buckets (e.g. events at 1h/2h/3h/4h/6h) written as 'highest threshold reached today' give a banded daily score. This is the only route to programmatic data. Inference: buckets, not minutes.

claims.claim: Individual authorization is supported: requestAuthorization(for: .individual) manages the current device (added iOS 16), no parent/child setup. Events must target apps/categories/web domains selected via FamilyActivityPicker (opaque tokens). I did not find a source stating that an 'all apps' event total is exact; selecting all categories is an inference.
claims.design_implication: Works for the two-person own-device case. User must pick apps/categories in the picker once; need to validate in a spike that selecting all categories yields a total close to Settings > Screen Time.

claims.claim: Threshold callbacks are unreliable: overcounting (300 min threshold fired at ~150 min on iOS 17.6.1, likely double-counting Safari and websites), callbacks firing with 0 minutes on iOS 26.2 (FB21450954), silent failures, repeat firing. Also the extension may not be woken exactly at crossing time.
claims.design_implication: Treat the data as untrusted-ish: use for coarse bands, show Apple's own report (or a manual confirm) as ground truth, don't award or deduct big points on a single threshold event. These are community reports, not Apple statements.

claims.claim: Family Controls is a privileged entitlement: you must request permission from Apple before distributing apps using it via TestFlight or App Store. Dev entitlement suffices only for Xcode-installed development builds (inference from Apple's model; no primary Apple page fetched confirming TestFlight specifically, but forum reporters had bundle IDs approved 'for an app I'm testing via TestFlight').
claims.design_implication: Plan for a distribution-entitlement request for the app AND each extension bundle ID (monitor, report, any shield) separately. Submit before building anything else on this path.

claims.claim: Approval timing is unpublished. Apple engineer said Apple provides no timelines. Reports: 2 days to a few days (best case), ~3 weeks typical, 31-33 days and 4.5 weeks, some stuck at 'Submitted' 4+ weeks with DTS tickets in early 2026. Each extension bundle ID needs its own request; multiple requests allowed.
claims.design_implication: Budget 1 to 6 weeks, with risk of indefinite wait. A personal two-user 'not for App Store' use case may be scrutinized; write a plain, genuine description (self-monitoring/digital wellbeing). Build the rest of the app so screen time is a pluggable module.

claims.claim: No Flutter plugin wraps DeviceActivity (monitor/report). flutter_family_controls 0.0.3 covers authorization, FamilyActivityPicker, ManagedSettings; app_blocker 2.1.0 uses FamilyControls+ManagedSettings shields; screen_time_api_ios is minimal; screen_time is Android-only. A DEV article recommends a custom MethodChannel.
claims.design_implication: Write your own small Swift plugin (picker + schedule start + App Group read) plus native extension targets in Xcode. Extensions are always Swift regardless of Flutter. Flutter plugins are low-version, thin; don't depend on them.

claims.claim: Shortcuts has no trigger or action exposing Screen Time totals or 'app limit ignored / extend time' events. Available app automation is 'App is opened/closed', which can start a timer or redirect. I found only blogs, no Apple doc; absence of a trigger is inferred from the lack of any listed one.
claims.design_implication: Do not rely on Shortcuts for usage totals. A Shortcut 'when app X opens, POST to server' can count opens of specific apps (e.g. social/video) as a cheap proxy, but it is user-removable and lacks duration.

claims.claim: Apple's Screen Time weekly report notification and Settings screen are not exposed to apps. I did not find any API reading them; the only programmatic route is the Screen Time API family.
claims.design_implication: Manual entry or screenshot OCR are the non-entitlement fallbacks.

findings.recommended_approach:
Ranked by effort vs reliability:

1. Zero-entitlement baseline, build first (low effort, high reliability, honest data): a daily/weekly manual check-in. Preferably a screenshot of Settings > Screen Time (daily average or yesterday) shared into the app; on-device OCR (Apple Vision via a small Flutter plugin, or google_mlkit_text_recognition) extracts the total and the 'Pickups' count, with a confirm/edit step. Both users see each other's number, which keeps it honest (social accountability replaces enforcement). Score on weekly average vs the user's own baseline (relative improvement), which also helps fairness between Nick and Nadia. Cost: roughly 15 seconds per day or per week. Weekly screenshot is enough for a 'beat last week' game.

2. Submit the Family Controls (Distribution) entitlement request now, in parallel, for app + DeviceActivityMonitor extension (+ report extension if wanted), each bundle ID, with a plain self-monitoring description. Costs nothing and the wait is 2 days to 6+ weeks. Meanwhile develop with the development entitlement on your own devices (works via Xcode install; TestFlight will not work until approved).

3. Once approved: DeviceActivityMonitor extension with a repeating daily schedule and threshold events (e.g. 1h, 2h, 3h, 4h, 5h, 6h) on a FamilyActivitySelection of all categories, writing the highest hit and timestamp to App Group UserDefaults; the host app syncs to the Go/Postgres or Next backend. Add a DeviceActivityReport view embedded in the app for the user's own detailed dashboard (display only). Treat hits as coarse bands and cross-check with the manual/OCR number; allow correction. Validate first in a 1 to 2 day spike that the all-categories event matches Settings within tolerance on iOS 26.

4. Optional cheap signal: Shortcuts personal automations 'when [Instagram/YouTube/TikTok] opens' that call your server webhook, giving open counts for 'bad' apps.

Architecture: in Flutter, put screen time behind a ScreenTimeSource interface with implementations Manual, Ocr, DeviceActivityBuckets so the scoring engine does not care which is active.
alternatives: Manual entry only: simplest, always works, relies on honesty; fine for two people who trust each other.
Screenshot OCR of Settings > Screen Time (Vision framework or ML Kit, with confirmation): near-zero entitlement risk, automates entry; layout may change between iOS versions so keep the edit step.
Weekly report screenshot instead of daily: lowest friction; pair with a Shortcut reminder.
Shortcuts app-open webhooks to count opens of distracting apps.
Skip screen time scoring and instead reward positive behaviors (audiobook minutes, reading) that are measurable elsewhere, with screen time as a self-reported stat.
Fully native Swift for just a small screen-time companion target while the rest stays Flutter (this is required anyway, since extensions are Swift).
cannot_do: Export exact minutes from DeviceActivityReport to the host app or server: Apple DTS says it is intentionally sandboxed.
Read Settings > Screen Time numbers, the weekly report notification, or per-app durations as data via any public API without the Family Controls route.
Get per-app minute breakdowns in your own code: apps are opaque tokens, only the Apple-rendered report shows names, and monitor events give only 'threshold reached' (inference from API shape).
Use Family Controls on TestFlight without Apple approving the distribution entitlement for each bundle ID; the timeline is unpredictable.

Detect 'ignore limit for today / one more minute' or password-entry events via Shortcuts; no such trigger found. A DeviceActivityMonitor intervalDidEnd / shield approach might approximate limit-bypass but would require shielding apps with ManagedSettings and was not verified.
Guarantee threshold accuracy: documented overcounting and spurious firings exist on iOS 17 through 26.2.
Verify the Family Controls flow in the iOS Simulator; a real device is required.
open_questions_for_user: Is it acceptable that the screen-time feature launches as manual/OCR and upgrades to automatic buckets only after Apple approves the entitlement (could be weeks)?
Are you willing to request the entitlement with a self-monitoring justification, accepting that rejection is possible for a private non-App-Store app?
Do you want to reward lowered total screen time, or only specific apps/categories (social, video)? That changes whether to use all-categories events or a curated selection.
Should scoring be relative to each person's own baseline (recommended for fairness given Nadia's job) rather than absolute hours?
Is a daily 15-second screenshot or entry check-in acceptable, or should it be weekly?
Do you have iOS 26.x on both phones, and are you OK with an extra Swift extension target inside the Flutter project?

verdicts.claim: 1. DeviceActivityReport extension intentionally sandboxed; DTS said Yes
verdicts.evidence: Fetched https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/818174 (DTS: 'Yes. See thread 817516') and https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/817516 (DTS Quinn, accepted answer 'Is Screen Time trapped inside DeviceActivityReport on purpose?' - 'Yes'; sensitive appexen run in a read-only sandbox so they cannot export data to less-restricted code; points to DeviceActivityReport doc comments).
verdicts.correction: None. Note the engineer says 'it certainly looks like' this includes report extensions, i.e. by analogy with Network Extension filters, plus the doc comments.

verdicts.claim: 2. Report view shows totals in host app but host never sees numbers; report extension fails to launch on some builds
verdicts.evidence: Sandbox part is supported by thread 817516 above. I did not fetch the launch-failure threads (821625, tag page), so that part is unverified.
verdicts.correction: Treat the 'fails to launch on some iOS 26.x builds' part as unverified anecdote.

verdicts.claim: 3. DeviceActivityMonitor can write to App Group; threshold events pattern; ~5 MB extension memory
verdicts.evidence: Apple docs https://developer.apple.com/documentation/deviceactivity/deviceactivitymonitor confirm the monitor extension concept. Search results also show a forum report of callbacks never firing with unusual schedule windows. I did not re-fetch Crunchybagel or confirm the 5 MB figure from a primary source.
verdicts.correction: Keep the pattern as the standard workaround but mark the 5 MB limit as community-reported, not Apple-documented, and flag schedule-window sensitivity.

verdicts.claim: 4. Individual authorization supported (.individual, iOS 16); events need FamilyActivityPicker tokens; 'all apps' exactness unverified
verdicts.evidence: Not re-verified against Apple docs in this pass. Nothing found contradicting it. Note one forum report (via search summary of the Family Controls tag) that on TestFlight the App and Website Usage capability showed .approved rather than approvedWithDataAccess seen in dev builds, which may affect behavior.
verdicts.correction: Keep as is, and add: validate on a TestFlight build, not only a dev build, because capability status may differ.

verdicts.claim: 5. Threshold callbacks unreliable (overcounting, 0-minute fires on iOS 26.2, silent failures)
verdicts.evidence: Not fetched. No primary source found either way. Multiple third-party and forum reports exist, so plausible, but unverified by me.
verdicts.correction: Keep the 'treat as coarse bands, cross-check with manual/OCR' stance.

verdicts.claim: 6. Family Controls is privileged; distribution entitlement needed for TestFlight
verdicts.evidence: Fetched https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/812332: OP had two bundle IDs approved 'for an app I'm testing via TestFlight'. No post in that thread states TestFlight requires it, and the only DTS reply just says to file a code-level support ticket. Search also surfaced https://newly.app/how-to/family-controls-entitlement and https://note.com/niki_ai/n/na8c9c4847174 (secondary).
verdicts.correction: State as 'strongly implied by practice and secondary sources, no Apple page stating TestFlight explicitly'. Plan as if required.

verdicts.claim: 7. Approval timing unpublished; wide range; each extension bundle ID needs own request
verdicts.evidence: Search of Apple forums 2026: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/818553 (submitted Mar 9 2026, no response), https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/821964 (10+ days pending), https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/820700 (parent app approved, extension IDs separately pending), thread 812332 (~3 weeks pending, DTS gives no timeline).
verdicts.correction: None, but the 'works within days' best case is anecdotal; the extension-specific stall (main app approved, extensions stuck in Submitted) is a notable risk to add.

verdicts.claim: 8. No Flutter plugin wraps DeviceActivity; flutter_family_controls 0.0.3; app_blocker 2.1.0; screen_time_api_ios minimal; screen_time Android-only; DEV article recommends MethodChannel
verdicts.evidence: https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_family_controls is now 0.0.5 (published ~47 days ago, unverified uploader, 331 downloads), still covering only authorization, FamilyActivityPicker, ManagedSettings shields, no DeviceActivity monitoring. Also found https://github.com/ioridev/flutter_screentime (Flutter plugin whose README says the host app adds a Device Activity Monitor extension, shared App Group, and ships DeviceActivityMonitorExtension.swift.sample templates) - a partial scaffold, not a full monitor/report wrapper. screen_time_api_ios latest 0.0.4 (~3 years old, stale) per https://pub.dev/packages/screen_time_api_ios/versions. screen_time is described as Android real-time monitoring (https://pub.dev/packages/screen_time). The DEV article URL is https://dev.to/es404020/building-a-custom-screen-time-flutter-app-with-ios-native-apis-4k9f (the claim cited eniolaajani, which differs). I did not verify app_blocker 2.1.0.
verdicts.correction: flutter_family_controls is 0.0.5, not 0.0.3. No package gives a typed Dart API over DeviceActivity monitoring/reporting, but ioridev/flutter_screentime offers extension templates worth reviewing. Conclusion stands: write the monitor extension natively in Swift and bridge via MethodChannel plus App Group.

verification.revised_recommendation: The recommendation largely stands. Key sandbox claim is confirmed by DTS. Keep the tiered plan: (1) build the manual/OCR screen-time baseline behind a ScreenTimeSource interface; (2) file Family Controls distribution requests now, one per bundle ID (app, DeviceActivityMonitor extension, and optional report extension), and expect the extension IDs to be the slow part, so budget weeks and file a DTS ticket with Team ID if stuck; (3) after approval, validate on an actual TestFlight build (not only Xcode dev builds) that threshold events and authorization status behave as in dev, since a forum report notes .approved vs approvedWithDataAccess differences; (4) write the monitor extension in native Swift with an App Group, bridged by MethodChannel, optionally starting from ioridev/flutter_screentime templates; use flutter_family_controls (0.0.5) only for authorization and the picker; (5) treat threshold hits as coarse bands and keep manual/OCR as the source of truth. Do not depend on the 5 MB limit or iOS 26 reliability claims until tested in the 1-2 day spike. The Shortcuts webhook idea is untouched by this pass (not checked).

findings.topic: Free/open nutrition data and food logging input for a private two-user iPhone app (Flutter + Go + Postgres, self-hosted)

claims.claim: USDA FoodData Central API: free, requires a data.gov API key; 1,000 requests/hour/IP default (429 and 1h block if exceeded); DEMO_KEY is 30/hr and 50/day. Endpoints: /food/{fdcId}, /foods, /foods/list, /foods/search. Data types: Foundation, SR Legacy, Survey (FNDDS), Experimental, Branded. Data is CC0 1.0 (public domain); credit is requested but not required. Keys must not be committed publicly.
claims.design_implication: The Go backend holds the key and proxies/caches; 1,000/hr is far beyond two users. Never ship the key in the Flutter app or a public repo. No license obligations, so USDA can be copied wholesale into Postgres.

claims.claim: USDA bulk downloads (release 04/2026 for Foundation and Branded): Foundation JSON 459K zipped/6.5M; Foundation CSV 3.7M/32M; SR Legacy (final, 04/2018, never updated) JSON 12.3M/205M, CSV 6.7M/54M; Branded JSON 195M zipped/3.1G unzipped, Branded CSV 428M/2.9G. The download page itself states no license, but the API guide states CC0.
claims.design_implication: Preload Foundation + SR Legacy (generic whole foods, small) fully into Postgres. Branded is optional: importing it (about 3 GB raw, a few hundred MB loaded after trimming to key nutrients plus GTIN/UPC, brand, serving size) gives offline US barcode lookup. Re-import is a twice-yearly cron job.

claims.claim: Branded Foods data quality: label-derived values supplied by manufacturers/Label Insight; includes gtin_upc, serving size, household serving text. I did not verify error rates or staleness in a source. Generally known to contain stale or reformulated products, which is inference, not verified here.
claims.design_implication: Treat branded matches as 'probably right', allow user edits, and let a scanned label override a stored branded record (user-corrected records win).

claims.claim: Open Food Facts API limits: product read 15 req/min per IP, search 10 req/min per IP (not for search-as-you-type, ban risk), global 503 limits; custom User-Agent 'AppName/Version (email)' required; reads need no auth. Product endpoint e.g. /api/v3.6/product/{barcode}.json. Full-text search is not in API v2 (use Search-a-licious). Requests made directly by users from a mobile app are limited per user.
claims.design_implication: Barcode lookup through the Go backend with a proper User-Agent is fine at 15/min for two users. Do not use OFF for text search; use local Postgres search instead. Cache every hit.

claims.claim: Open Food Facts dumps: MongoDB dump, JSONL (openfoodfacts-products.jsonl.gz), Parquet (food.parquet on Hugging Face, simplified), CSV (en.openfoodfacts.org.products.csv.gz, tab-separated, about 0.9 GB gz / 9 GB unzipped), RDF (experimental). Daily deltas cover the previous 14 days. Total product count not stated on the page.
claims.design_implication: Do not preload the whole OFF dump; it is global and large. If wanted, filter the Parquet/JSONL to countries_tags contains en:united-states with nutriments present and load only that subset. Otherwise live lookup by barcode plus caching is enough.

claims.claim: OFF licensing: database under ODbL, contents under DbCL, images CC BY-SA. Requested attribution: 'Contains data from Open Food Facts, available under the Open Database License'. ODbL share-alike applies to public use/distribution of derived databases; a private two-person app is not a public use. My reading of ODbL as not triggering obligations for private use is inference, not stated on the page.
claims.design_implication: Store OFF-sourced rows with a source='off' tag and put an attribution line in an About screen. Keep OFF records distinguishable so any later public release could comply or purge them.

claims.claim: OFF US coverage: no authoritative US count found. Mirror snapshots of country tag pages show only about 1.7k-1.9k products tagged United States, but these are from community mirrors with inconsistent tagging and cannot be trusted as a total. Actual US barcode coverage was not verified.
claims.design_implication: Do not assume OFF covers US products well. Measure it: before building, test 30 to 50 barcodes from your actual pantry against OFF and USDA Branded and pick the order by hit rate. Plan for a frequent miss and a label-scan fallback.

claims.claim: I did not find OFF 'Open Prices' or image-OCR feature details in this research pass (not fetched). Not a dependency for this design.
claims.design_implication: Ignore for v1. Revisit only if you want price tracking for grocery cost; contribute-back to OFF is optional.

claims.claim: Nutritionix: sources conflict. A June 2026 competitor blog says the free developer tier is gone, with paid plans from about $499/month; older sources claim 50-200 calls/day free. Treat as not available.
claims.design_implication: Do not depend on Nutritionix.

claims.claim: FatSecret Platform API Basic edition: free self-serve, 5,000 calls/day per key, US dataset, community support; mandatory attribution; cached content not marked storable-indefinitely must be removed or re-requested within 24h. Premier Free (startups/non-profits/students, verification) adds barcode scanning and autocomplete, still with attribution. Barcode is not in Basic.
claims.design_implication: Usable as an optional live text-search supplement for restaurant/chain items but the 24h cache rule means you cannot build your own database from it. Low priority; USDA branded plus OFF covers most needs.

claims.claim: Edamam and CalorieNinjas free-tier numbers could not be verified from primary sources. Edamam secondary sources say a free tier exists scaling to about $49/month; CalorieNinjas has a keyed free plan with a monthly quota (numbers unverified).
claims.design_implication: Skip both. They add terms/quotas risk without covering anything USDA + OFF + LLM parsing do not. CalorieNinjas-style natural-language parsing ('2 eggs and toast') can be replaced by your own LLM call.

claims.claim: Barcode scanning: mobile_scanner 7.4.2 (about 42 days old at fetch) uses AVFoundation/Apple Vision on iOS, not ML Kit, so no ML Kit pod weight on iOS. Open issues exist: black preview up to about 1 min after a system language change (Oct 2026), accelerometer read on launch since 7.4.1 (#1801), close-range focus problems on Pro iPhones (workaround: getBestCloseRangeScanningLens()). No confirmed iOS 26 breakage found, but also no explicit iOS 26 confirmation.
claims.design_implication: Use mobile_scanner for UPC/EAN; enable close-range lens selection; test on both real iPhones early. Keep a manual barcode-number entry field as a fallback.

claims.claim: google_mlkit_text_recognition 0.17.1 (published about 2 months before fetch): iOS min deployment target 15.5, Xcode 15.3+, 64-bit only (exclude armv7), Latin script by default. A search result noted ML Kit historically lacks arm64 iOS simulator slices and Xcode 26 dropped Rosetta simulators; the Flutter plugin status for this was NOT confirmed.
claims.design_implication: Prefer a thin Apple Vision (VNRecognizeTextRequest) platform channel or the community Vision-based plugin for OCR so simulator dev works and no Google pod is needed; or skip on-device OCR entirely and send the photo to a vision LLM (below). Verify the simulator question by building a spike on Xcode 26 before committing.

claims.claim: LLM-based label parsing: no authoritative per-image cost figure found; third-party sources list Claude Sonnet 4.6 at $3/$15 per M tokens and Gemini 2.5 Flash at $0.30/$2.50. Both support image input and structured JSON output. I did not verify accuracy on nutrition labels. Cost for a few labels per week is negligible either way.
claims.design_implication: Send the label photo directly to a vision model with a strict JSON schema (serving size, servings per container, calories, macros, sodium, fiber, sugars, added sugars) from the Go backend. Validate with arithmetic checks (4/4/9 kcal rule within tolerance, %DV sanity) and show a confirm screen with the photo beside parsed values. Use regex over OCR only as an offline fallback.

claims.claim: Recipes: Spoonacular official free plan is 50 points/day, 1 req/s, 402 after quota (third-party sites claim 150, official page takes priority); points not equal to requests. TheMealDB: free V1 with test key '1', free for dev/education, publicly released apps require supporter upgrade, free list results limited to 100, multi-ingredient filter is premium; small catalog, not US-centric nutrition. Mealie: self-hosted, long-lived API tokens, interactive API docs at /docs, shopping lists with API-only extras; Tandoor: OpenAPI 3 spec at /openapi/ on each instance, covers recipes, meal plans, shopping lists, URL scraping (third-party aggregator claim).
claims.design_implication: Do not build on Spoonacular's 50 points/day or TheMealDB's small catalog. Either run Mealie in the same Docker Compose (URL scraping, meal plan, shopping list with an API) and have the app consume its API, or keep recipes in your own Postgres tables with an LLM-based 'paste URL or photo to import' step. Mealie meal-plan and URL-import endpoint details were not verified here.

findings.recommended_approach:
Layered lookup, all behind the Go API with a single local Postgres food table (source, source_id, gtin, name, brand, per-serving and per-100g nutrients, serving options, verified flag, created_by). 

PRELOAD at deploy time: USDA Foundation + SR Legacy (tiny, CC0) for generic foods and ingredients with Postgres full-text/trigram search. Optionally USDA Branded trimmed to GTIN, brand, name, serving size, and core nutrients (about 3 GB raw to import once, twice-yearly refresh) for offline US barcode hits.

QUERY LIVE and CACHE FOREVER: barcode scan goes local gtin match, then USDA Branded API search by GTIN if not preloaded, then Open Food Facts /product/{barcode} (User-Agent set, 15/min is plenty), writing every hit into the local table as source-tagged rows. Text search is always local (never OFF search, never search-as-you-type against remote APIs).

SCAN when nothing matches: photograph the Nutrition Facts panel (and optionally the barcode number), send to a vision LLM from the backend with a strict JSON schema, validate with calorie-from-macros arithmetic, show a confirm/edit screen, save as a user-verified record keyed to the barcode so the miss never happens twice. Optional: contribute back to OFF later.

FINAL FALLBACK: quick-add (name plus calories plus optional macros) and a manual custom-food form, plus an LLM 'describe your meal' estimate flagged as approximate. Copy-from-recent and favorites cut repeated entry for a two-person household.

RECIPES: run Mealie in the same Docker Compose (URL import, meal plan, shopping list, API) or store recipes in your own tables; compute recipe nutrition by mapping ingredients to the local food table, and use pantry/'cook at home' logic in your own service. Avoid Spoonacular/TheMealDB as the core.

Use Tandoor instead of Mealie for the recipe manager (OpenAPI at /openapi/), or build recipes natively in Postgres to avoid a second service.

findings.topic: Exercise databases and workout program generation for two people (Nick and Nadia) with different schedules and equipment

claims.claim: free-exercise-db (yuhonas) is Unlicense (public domain), 876 exercises in dist/exercises.json (README says 800+), one JSON per exercise with id, name, force, level, mechanic, equipment, primaryMuscles, secondaryMuscles, instructions, category, images (static JPGs, no GIFs).
claims.design_implication: Use as the primary seed catalog, vendored into the repo and imported into Postgres. No license friction, no network dependency, images can be self-hosted.

claims.claim: free-exercise-db distribution (I computed this from the JSON): category strength 584, stretching 123, plyometrics 61, powerlifting 38, olympic 35, strongman 21, cardio 14. Equipment: barbell 170, dumbbell 123, other 122, body only 111, cable 81, null 77, machine 67, kettlebells 56, bands 20. Level: beginner 525, intermediate 294, expert 57. 17 muscle groups (abdominals, abductors, adductors, biceps, calves, chest, forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lats, lower back, middle back, neck, quadriceps, shoulders, traps, triceps). force/mechanic can be null (30/87), equipment null for 77.

Muscle taxonomy is coarse (no rear delt/front delt split, no hip flexor), so own a normalized muscle map for volume counting.

claims.claim: Coverage gaps in free-exercise-db for this household: it has pull-ups (Pullups, Band Assisted Pull-Up, Scapular Pull-Up, Weighted Pull Ups, Hanging Leg Raise), treadmill entries (Running/Jogging/Walking, Treadmill) in cardio, and 123 stretching items including Child's Pose and Cat Stretch, but there is no yoga category/flow, no climbing-specific training (hangboard, antiforearm extensor, campus), and only 'One Handed Hang' and 'Rope Climb' as nearby items. Pull-up bar is not an equipment value (likely 'other' or 'body only'), so exercises needing it must be tagged manually.
claims.design_implication: Add a small hand-curated overlay table (extra exercises + equipment tags: pull_up_bar, treadmill, living_room_mat, climbing_gym) layered on top of the imported catalog. Treat running and yoga as separate modules, not rows in the strength catalog.

claims.claim: ExerciseDB (exercisedb-api repo) is AGPL-3.0 code; README claims 11,000+ exercises, 15,000+ videos, 20,000+ images, 5,000+ GIFs. Fields in V2 sample: exerciseId, name, imageUrl, equipments, bodyParts, gender, exerciseType, targetMuscles, secondaryMuscles, videoUrl, keywords, overview, instructions, exerciseTips, variations, relatedExerciseIds. REST API at /api/v2/ with OpenAPI schema at /api/v2/schema, public endpoints readable without auth, 20 results per page default, exercise endpoints not throttled. Self-hostable via docker compose. I could not verify exercise count (a third-party scraper listing says 800+) or the exact exercise/exerciseinfo field list; the wger.de site blocks bots with Anubis.
