(5) Treat smart-toothbrush HealthKit ingestion as optional, pending the brush they own. Items 5 and 7 were not independently verified here."

findings.topic: Sleep and wake-up scoring from Apple Watch / HealthKit data (iOS 26), for a two-person habit app

claims.claim: HealthKit exposes sleep as one category type, sleepAnalysis. Values: inBed, awake, asleepCore (light/intermediate), asleepDeep, asleepREM, asleepUnspecified (stage unknown), deprecated asleep. A static set allAsleepValues exists for predicates. Each sample has one value. inBed samples overlap the detailed stage samples, and the stage samples do not overlap each other.
claims.design_implication: Build the asleep timeline as the union of allAsleepValues samples. Never sum raw sample durations because overlapping sources cause double counting. Merge samples from multiple sources by taking the union, or pick one source per user.

claims.claim: Apple's docs say samples recorded by Apple Watch only include 'awake' samples that occur BETWEEN two sleep samples. There may be no detailed samples at the start or end of an inBed sample. So the final awake period before getting up is NOT represented as awake, and the last asleep sample's endDate is the wake time. Sleep latency and the real out-of-bed time cannot be derived from Watch samples alone.
claims.design_implication: Define sleep_onset = start of first asleep sample and wake_time = end of last asleep sample in the main session. Do not compute sleep latency or time awake in bed after waking from Watch data. Use inBed only as a weak hint, because it may come from the phone's Bedtime schedule.

claims.claim: Stage and quality caveats. An integration vendor's doc reports binary asleep/awake is written for sessions of 1-3 h, and full stages only above 3 h (single secondary source). Apple Watch sleep-stage samples are written as a batch after the session ends and post-processing completes (Apple DTS answer), not incrementally, and can show up in HealthKit many minutes after waking. Stage estimation uses accelerometer plus heart rate; Apple publishes a validation PDF (Oct 2025) that I could not read because the fetch exceeded the size limit.
claims.design_implication: Compute the nightly score lazily. Use an HKObserverQuery with enableBackgroundDelivery and an anchored query, and finalize the night's score only once the session samples settle (for example 15-30 min after the last sample arrives, or on next app open). Do not promise real-time wake detection. Use only timing and total sleep for the core score and keep deep/REM out of points.

claims.claim: Other overnight HealthKit types that exist (verified in the identifier listings): respiratoryRate, heartRate, restingHeartRate, heartRateVariabilitySDNN, walkingHeartRateAverage, appleSleepingWristTemperature, appleSleepingBreathingDisturbances, stepCount, oxygenSaturation, timeInDaylight. Wrist temperature needs Series 8+/Ultra/SE3 and about 5 nights of Sleep Focus-based baseline setup (Apple support). A dev-forum report says the HealthKit sample carries only the absolute value, with no baseline or deflection metadata (unverified). I found no documentation that respiratoryRate or heartRate are tagged as sleeping values; they are ordinary samples you window by the sleep session times.
claims.design_implication: For recovery context, compute overnight means of HR, HRV and respiratory rate inside [sleep_onset, wake_time] and compare with each person's own 14-28 day baseline. Show these as informational chips, not in the points formula. Wrist temp and breathing disturbances are optional and device-dependent.

claims.claim: The watchOS 26 Sleep Score does not appear in HealthKit: the full HKQuantityTypeIdentifier and HKCategoryTypeIdentifier listings on developer.apple.com contain no sleep-score type. The Health app computes it (retroactively, from existing sleep data including third-party sources). Components: duration 50, bedtime 30, interruptions 20 points. Bands changed in watchOS 26.2 beta to Very Low 0-40, Low 41-60, OK 61-80, High 81-95, Very High 96-100 (26.0 had Excellent 90-100). I could not confirm the final shipped bands.
claims.design_implication: The app must compute its own sleep score from sleepAnalysis. Mirror Apple's public 50/30/20 split idea (duration, bedtime, interruptions) so the number feels familiar. Do not promise to display Apple's own score. The 'no HealthKit type' finding is high confidence; the band numbers are medium (press sources only).

claims.claim: Sleep Regularity Index (SRI), verified from the Phillips 2017 paper: the probability that a person is in the same asleep/awake state at two time points 24 h apart, evaluated minute by minute and averaged over all days, rescaled with y = 200(x - 1/2) to run -100 to 100 (100 periodic, 0 random). It does not require designating a main sleep episode, so naps and all-nighters are handled. In the study the Regular versus Irregular quintile had melatonin onset about 2.5 h earlier, and SRI correlated with GPA (r = 0.37). Observational, 61 students, sleep diaries.
claims.design_implication: SRI is directly computable from the asleep-union timeline at 1-minute resolution. Use a trailing window of 7 days for display and 14 days for stability. Use the 0-100 form, SRI = 100 * P(same state), matching Sleep Cycle's and the UK Biobank paper's scale.

claims.claim: UK Biobank evidence (n=88,975, 7-day wrist accelerometry). SRI has a non-linear relation to mortality. Median SRI is 60 (SD 10), 5th percentile 41, 95th percentile 75. All-cause HR is 1.53 at the 5th percentile and 0.90 at the 95th, relative to the median. After adjusting for BMI, BP and activity the 5th-percentile HR is 1.22. A separate analysis (Windred 2024, n=60,977) reports regularity as a stronger predictor than duration. Limits: observational, single week of exposure, inferred sleep, mostly older White cohort, reverse causation possible.
claims.design_implication: Map SRI to points using empirical anchors: 0 pts at SRI <= 41, full points at SRI >= 75, linear between. These are accelerometer-based population percentiles, so label them targets, not clinical thresholds. Make no health claims in the UI. Numbers are high confidence; causal interpretation is medium.

claims.claim: Social jetlag (SJL) is the difference between the midpoint of sleep on free days and on work days (Wittmann/Roenneberg 2006; the MCTQ docs define relative SJL as MSF - MSW). The sleep-corrected MSFsc is part of the MCTQ literature but I could not retrieve its formula. Sleep Cycle uses a practical version: weekday-to-weekend wake-time gap, under 1 h as target and over 2 h flagged as social jetlag.
claims.design_implication: Compute SJL = |median free-day midpoint - median work-day midpoint| over a trailing 28 days with at least 4 free-day nights (skip otherwise). The work/free split should come from each person's own configured schedule (Nadia works weekdays, Nick works from home). Use it as a weekly modifier only. Flag that MSFsc's formula was not verified.

claims.claim: There is no public iOS 'got out of bed' signal. HealthKit has none, and Apple Watch samples omit the trailing awake time. I found nothing documenting first-unlock as a readable event, and iOS has no public first-unlock callback (my inference; not found documented). Plausible proxies, all inference and unverified: (a) end of last asleep sample, (b) first stepCount sample after wake_time, (c) first HR above the person's resting baseline. RISE reportedly uses first phone pickup in the morning and last at night (Built In article; mechanism unverified).
claims.design_implication: Treat wake_time (end of last asleep sample) as the objective wake signal. Add a get-moving latency = time from wake_time to first 20+ step burst, as an optional low-weight bonus with a sanity cap. Latency will often be near 0 because Apple's session usually ends once the wearer is moving, and steps from a phone in another room add noise. Never penalize a missing or late signal.

claims.claim: AlarmKit (iOS 26+, iPhone/iPad) lets an app schedule prominent alarms and timers that can break through Silent/Focus, with snooze and countdown. But the app cannot reliably tell if or when the user dismissed an alarm: swiping away doesn't call the stop intent; the stopIntent LiveActivityIntent fires for the on-screen Stop button but not when the user dismisses by interacting with the unlocked screen or the Live Activity banner (reproduced on iOS 26.2.1 per forum); AlarmManager alarm updates don't expose a 'dismissed' state. An Apple DTS engineer asked for a repro and said they hadn't seen the issue. Mostly single-developer reports.
claims.design_implication: AlarmKit is useful for delivering a wake alarm and for a self-declared 'alarm set' habit, but not as a measurement tool. Score off HealthKit wake time. The stop intent may be recorded as a bonus signal, but missing events must never reduce a score.

claims.claim: Third-party consistency approaches. Sleep Cycle's newer score has three pillars (Duration, Quality, Routine) with Routine the biggest weight (no numeric weights published); Routine uses SRI plus weekday/weekend wake gap and advises wake variation under 1 h. WHOOP's sleep consistency is a 0-100% measure of bed/wake time similarity over roughly the last 4-5 nights (community report, not official). SleepScore (sleep.ai) uses deviation from average bed/wake time. COROS includes bedtime consistency as one of six factors. Oura's Sleep Score contributors include total sleep, efficiency, latency, restfulness and timing (personalized ideal bedtime); no consistency formula or weights found. RISE uses sleep debt plus a circadian-based energy schedule. I found no usable AutoSleep documentation.
claims.design_implication: Copy the pattern: weight consistency at least as much as duration, measure it as deviation from the person's own recent norm, and judge over 7-14 days rather than a single night. Do not copy any vendor's undocumented weights.

claims.claim: Fairness reasoning (not researched, no study on couple-based comparative sleep scoring found). Consistency metrics (SRI, deviation from own median) are relative to each person's own routine, so they do not reward free time. Duration needs a personal target and an upper cap because sleeping long is not a habit to reward.
claims.design_implication: Each person sets target wake window and sleep need (default 7.5 h, range 7-9 h). Points come from adherence to their own targets, never raw hours. For head-to-head, compare percent-of-max or streak length, not minutes of sleep.

findings.recommended_approach:
RECOMMENDED SLEEP SCORING MODEL (computed from HealthKit sleepAnalysis; Apple's Sleep Score is not needed and not available)

Definitions per person, per night (sleep day runs noon to noon, local time):
- A = union of all asleep samples (allAsleepValues) across sources at 1-minute epochs. In-bed-only and awake gaps are not asleep.
- Main session = longest cluster of A, merging gaps under 60 min.
- onset = start of session; wake = end of session (end of last asleep sample).
- TST = minutes asleep inside the session. TIB = wake - first inBed start if present, else wake - onset.
- Per-person targets (editable): need N (default 450 min), target wake W* with flex band, target bedtime B*. Workday and free-day targets can differ.

NIGHTLY SCORE, 0-100:
1. Duration (30): 30 * clamp(TST / N, 0, 1). If TST > N + 90 min, subtract 30 * (TST - (N + 90)) / 120, floor 15 (no reward for oversleeping).
2. Wake-time consistency (25): dev_w = circular minutes between wake and the trailing 7-night median wake. 25 * (1 - clamp((dev_w - 30) / 90, 0, 1)). Full within 30 min, zero at 120+.
3. Bedtime consistency (15): same with onset; full within 45 min, zero at 150+ (dev_b - 45) / 105.
4. Interruptions (15): n = awake gaps over 5 min inside the session (the only awake data Apple writes). 15 - min(15, 3n). Optional efficiency = TST/TIB term: 0 below 80%, full above 90%.
5. Morning (15): Up-on-time U = 10 * (1 - clamp((|wake - W*| - 15) / 75, 0, 1)). Get-moving M = 5 if first 20+ step burst occurs within 30 min of wake (unvalidated proxy), else 0. If step data is missing, give those 5 points to U (no penalty).
A night is 'slept well' (streak-eligible) at score >= 70. A night with no data (Watch not worn) is a neutral skip: no points, and the streak is not broken for up to 1 night per week.

WEEKLY SCORE:
- SRI_7 = 100 * fraction of minutes where state(t) == state(t - 24h) over the trailing 7 days (14 days once available). R = 40 * clamp((SRI_7 - 41) / (75 - 41), 0, 1).
- SJL_h = |median free-day midpoint - median work-day midpoint| (hours, trailing 28 days, needs 4+ free nights). Penalty P = 10 * clamp(SJL_h - 1, 0, 1), i.e. full penalty at 2 h or more.
- Weekly sleep points = R + 0.4 * mean(nightly score) + 20 - P, where the flat 20 is a base for participation (tune as needed), floored at zero.

Fairness: all targets are per person; consistency is relative to own median; oversleeping earns nothing extra; head-to-head compares percent of own max or streak length; separate workday and free-day templates for Nadia.

DATA REQUIRED (HealthKit read): sleepAnalysis (required); stepCount (optional, get-moving bonus); heartRate, restingHeartRate, heartRateVariabilitySDNN, respiratoryRate, appleSleepingWristTemperature, appleSleepingBreathingDisturbances (optional, informational chips only). Also per-person targets, work/free-day schedule, and the timezone offset stored with each night. Enable background delivery on sleepAnalysis and finalize a night 15-30 min after the last sample arrives or on next app open.

OPTIONAL: AlarmKit alarm to help hit W*. Record the stop-intent time only as a soft signal; never score on it.

Note: the point weights, thresholds (30/90 min bands, 70 cutoff) are my design choices, not research-derived; only the SRI anchors (41/75) and the 1-hour consistency and 1-2 hour SJL guidance come from sources.
alternatives: Self-report one-tap morning check-in ('up by target?') instead of or alongside the step proxy: simple and unambiguous, but honor-system, which is reasonable between a couple.
Use only a weekly SRI-style number (as Sleep Cycle weights Routine highest) with no per-night score: simplest and best evidenced, but gives less daily feedback for streaks.
Compute MSFsc-corrected social jetlag instead of the simple midpoint gap: more precise, but its formula was not verified here.
Use Screen Time / DeviceActivity for first-pickup wake detection (as RISE reportedly does): not researched here and likely needs the Family Controls entitlement; verify before committing.
Ask users to screenshot Apple's Sleep Score: rejected, since it is not in HealthKit and cannot be automated.
cannot_do: Cannot read the watchOS 26 Sleep Score from HealthKit: no such type exists in the HKQuantity or HKCategory identifier lists.
Cannot get real-time sleep stages or detect sleep onset or wake live: Apple Watch writes sleep samples in a batch after the session, possibly many minutes after waking.

Cannot get a true 'out of bed' time: HealthKit exposes none, Watch samples omit the trailing awake period, and I found no documented iOS first-unlock API. Wake time is the end of the last asleep sample and the step-latency proxy is unvalidated.
Cannot reliably detect AlarmKit alarm dismissal: swipe and banner dismissals don't fire the stop intent and no 'dismissed' state is exposed (iOS 26.2.1 reports).
Cannot compute sleep latency from Watch data alone, because leading awake time is not written.
Cannot vouch for deep/REM accuracy: Apple's validation PDF could not be read (fetch exceeded size limit), so stage minutes are treated as estimates.
Cannot confirm WHOOP, Oura, AutoSleep, RISE or Sleep Cycle internal formulas and weights: none are published in the sources found.
open_questions_for_user: Do both of you wear the Watch to bed every night? Missing nights change how forgiving the streak rules need to be.
Are you OK with an honor-system morning check-in ('I was up by target') as a backup when step data is missing?
What are your target wake windows for workdays and free days, and should Nadia's early horse mornings count as workdays?
Do you want a nightly sleep streak (score >= 70) or the weekly SRI-based consistency score as the headline?
Do you want AlarmKit alarms inside the app (iOS 26+ only), or will you keep your current alarm clock?
Should the social jetlag penalty be allowed to push weekly sleep points below zero, or be floored at zero?
Does either of you have a sleep condition or medication that should change the 7.5 h default need?

verdicts.claim: 1. sleepAnalysis category type; values inBed/awake/asleepCore/Deep/REM/Unspecified, deprecated asleep, static allAsleepValues; one value per sample; inBed overlaps stage samples, stages do not overlap each other.
verdicts.evidence: Apple page (fetched .md, copyright 2026): 'Each sleep analysis sample can have only one value'; 'detailed samples overlap the in-bed sample, but they don't overlap each other'; all cases and deprecated 'asleep' listed; allAsleepValues is Set<HKCategoryValueSleepAnalysis>. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit/hkcategoryvaluesleepanalysis.md. Not verified in the page: the exact membership of allAsleepValues (the page only says 'possible stages of sleep'; Core/Deep/REM/Unspecified is the widely understood contents). Sleep is the only sleep category type besides mindfulSession in the Mindfulness and Sleep group (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit/hkcategorytypeidentifier.md).
verdicts.correction: Add a caveat: no-overlap holds within one source's detailed samples. Multiple sources (Watch plus a third-party app) can produce overlapping asleep samples, so the union-at-1-minute-epoch approach in the recommendation is still needed.

verdicts.claim: 2. Watch-recorded samples only include awake samples between two sleep samples; the final awake period is not represented; the last asleep endDate is the wake time; sleep latency and out-of-bed time cannot be derived from Watch samples alone.
verdicts.evidence: Apple note, verbatim: 'Samples recorded by Apple Watch only include awake samples that occur between two sleep samples... there might not be any detailed samples that correspond to the beginning or ending of an in-bed sample.' Same URL as claim 1. However, the same page also says apps can compute 'the amount of time it took for the user to fall asleep' by comparing in-bed and detailed sample times.
verdicts.correction: Soften the last sentence. 'Cannot be derived' is an inference. Apple presents latency as derivable from inBed start vs first asleep start, but the Watch's inBed and the first-asleep boundaries are estimates and the leading and trailing gaps may be absent. Treat latency and out-of-bed time as unreliable or optional, not impossible. 'Last asleep endDate is the wake time' is also an inference (reasonable).

verdicts.claim: 3. Binary asleep/awake for 1-3 h sessions and full stages only above 3 h (single vendor source); Watch stage samples are written as a batch after the session ends (DTS); accelerometer plus heart rate; Apple validation PDF Oct 2025 unread.
verdicts.evidence: DTS part confirmed: accepted DTS answer says samples are 'not written to the local HealthKit store incrementally during sleep' but in a batch after the session ends once post-processing completes; there is no real-time API. https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/849362. The 'many minutes after waking' delay is not stated in what I read (inference). I did not fetch the vendor doc (mydatahelps) or the Apple PDF, so the 1-3 h and 3 h thresholds and the sensor claim stay unverified.
verdicts.correction: Keep: 'batch-written after session end, no incremental or real-time access (DTS)'. Mark the 1-3 h and 3 h thresholds as single-vendor, unverified. Do not hard-code them. The design already handles missing stages by using allAsleepValues, which is fine.

verdicts.claim: 4. Other overnight HealthKit types exist (respiratoryRate, heartRate, restingHeartRate, HRV SDNN, walkingHeartRateAverage, appleSleepingWristTemperature, appleSleepingBreathingDisturbances, stepCount, oxygenSaturation, timeInDaylight); wrist temp needs Series 8+/Ultra/SE3 and about 5 nights; HealthKit sample has only absolute value (unverified); no sleeping tag on respiratoryRate/heartRate.
verdicts.evidence: All listed identifiers appear in https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit/hkquantityidentifier.md (actual: .../hkquantitytypeidentifier.md). appleSleepingWristTemperature ('records the wrist temperature during sleep') and appleSleepingBreathingDisturbances are under 'Mindfulness and Sleep'. Apple support: wrist temp needs Series 8 or later, any Ultra, or SE 3; sleep tracking on; Sleep Focus on at least 4 hours per night for roughly 5 nights to establish baseline. https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT213275. The no-baseline-metadata point and 'no sleeping tag' remain unverified.
verdicts.correction: Add: the listing also contains heartRateVariabilityRMSSD (new alongside SDNN), and other sleep-adjacent types. Note the baseline needs Sleep Focus of 4+ hours per night, not just any sleep tracking. Keep the unverified items labelled.

verdicts.claim: 5. watchOS 26 Sleep Score is not in HealthKit; components 50/30/20; 26.2 bands Very Low 0-40, Low 41-60, OK 61-80, High 81-95, Very High 96-100 (26.0 had Excellent 90-100); final shipped bands unconfirmed.
verdicts.evidence: No sleep-score identifier in either the quantity or category identifier listings fetched (Apple .md pages above); a developer forum post also says no API exists (via search summary, secondary). Sleep Score is computed from third-party data too (https://9to5mac.com/2025/09/10/psa-the-new-sleep-score-feature-works-with-third-party-devices/). Components 50/30/20 per Macworld summary. Final bands: watchOS 26.2 released with exactly these bands (https://m.gsmarena.com/apple_watchos_26_2_update_released-news-70706.php); old bands were 0-29/30-49/50-69/70-89/90-100 (https://9to5mac.com/2025/11/04/watchos-26-2-sleep-score-changes-apple-watch/).
verdicts.correction: Change 'could not confirm shipped bands' to 'shipped in watchOS 26.2 (Dec 2025): Very Low 0-40, Low 41-60, OK 61-80, High 81-95, Very High 96-100'. Old 26.0 bands: Very Low 0-29, Low 30-49, OK 50-69, High 70-89, Excellent 90-100. Absence from the identifier listings is only as strong as those pages, but no contrary evidence found.

verdicts.claim: 6. SRI definition (Phillips 2017): same-state probability 24 h apart, rescaled 200(x-1/2) to -100..100; no main sleep episode needed; Regular vs Irregular quintile melatonin onset about 2.5 h earlier; SRI vs GPA r = 0.37; 61 students, diaries.
verdicts.evidence: Nature page redirected to a cookie-auth wall and the Harvard DASH PDF was not fetched, so I could not check the 2.5 h, r = 0.37 or n = 61 figures. The SRI definition and rescaling are consistent with the well-known formulation, but not verified by me in this session.
verdicts.correction: Keep the definition (high prior), but flag 2.5 h, r = 0.37 and n = 61 as carried over from the earlier researcher and not re-verified. These are context numbers only and do not affect the scoring model.

verdicts.claim: 7. UK Biobank SRI (n = 88,975): median 60 (SD 10), P5 41, P95 75; all-cause HR 1.53 at P5, 0.90 at P95 vs median; adjusted P5 HR 1.22; Windred 2024 (n = 60,977) says regularity is a stronger predictor than duration.
verdicts.evidence: eLife (https://elifesciences.org/articles/88359): n = 88,975; median 60 (text also says 61 in places), SD 10, P5 41, P95 75; HR 1.53 (1.41-1.66) at P5 and 0.90 (0.81-1.00) at P95. Model 4 P5 HR is 1.22 in the Results text but 1.20 (1.11-1.31) in an appendix figure caption; P95 Model 4 is 1.00 (0.90-1.12), i.e. the benefit disappears after full adjustment. Windred: https://academic.oup.com/sleep/article/47/1/zsad253/7280269 - abstract n = 60,977 (text also shows 60,997), conclusion regularity stronger than duration; adding duration to the regularity model did not significantly improve fit.
verdicts.correction: Note median is 60 or 61 and the adjusted P5 HR is 1.20-1.22. Add that the 'benefit' at P95 (HR 0.90) is not significant after full adjustment (HR 1.00). The 41 and 75 anchors used in the weekly R term are valid. These are population percentiles from older accelerometry, so treat them as a rough scale.

verdicts.claim: 8. Social jetlag = difference between free-day and work-day sleep midpoints (Wittmann/Roenneberg 2006; MCTQ relative SJL = MSF - MSW); MSFsc formula not retrieved; Sleep Cycle uses weekday-weekend wake gap, under 1 h target and over 2 h flagged.
verdicts.evidence: Not re-fetched in this pass (Wikipedia, ropensci mctq docs and Sleep Cycle page unchecked). The definition is consistent with standard MCTQ literature, but the Sleep Cycle 1 h and 2 h thresholds are unverified by me.
verdicts.correction: Keep the definition. Note the standard SJL is absolute |MSF - MSW| and, in the standard form, uses the sleep-corrected MSFsc to remove oversleep debt on free days. The researcher's plain-midpoint version over-penalizes people who sleep in to catch up. Label the 1 h and 2 h thresholds as design choices unless Sleep Cycle's page is confirmed.

verification.revised_recommendation: The scoring model largely stands. Revisions: (1) Do not rely on sleep latency or true out-of-bed time. Apple says latency can be derived from inBed vs detailed samples, but Watch samples may lack leading and trailing detail, so treat these as optional soft signals. Wake = end of last asleep sample stays. (2) Union asleep samples across sources at 1-minute epochs. The no-overlap guarantee only holds within one source's detailed samples. (3) Finalize each night only after the batch write, e.g. via background delivery on sleepAnalysis plus a 15-30 min quiet period or on next app open. DTS confirms there is no incremental or real-time stage data, so no live smart-alarm logic. (4) Sleep Score is not exposed via HealthKit (listings show no such identifier). Computing your own score is correct. If you want to mirror Apple's output bands in the UI, use the shipped 26.2 bands: Very Low 0-40, Low 41-60, OK 61-80, High 81-95, Very High 96-100. (5) SRI anchors 41 and 75 are fine (eLife P5 and P95). Cite the adjusted P5 HR as about 1.20-1.22 and note the P95 benefit is null after full adjustment. (6) Social jetlag: use MSFsc (sleep-corrected free-day midpoint) or at least do not penalize free-day oversleep recovery. The plain midpoint difference as written can penalize catching up on sleep. The 1 h and 2 h penalty thresholds are design choices. (7) Wrist temperature and breathing disturbances stay informational. Wrist temperature needs Series 8+/Ultra/SE3 plus Sleep Focus 4+ h for about 5 nights. HRV RMSSD now also exists as an identifier. (8) Unverified: Phillips 2017 numbers (2.5 h, r = 0.37, n = 61), the vendor 1-3 h and 3 h thresholds, the Apple PDF, and the Sleep Cycle thresholds. None are load-bearing for the model. Sources: Apple HealthKit .md pages, forums thread 849362, eLife 88359, OUP Sleep zsad253, GSMArena and 9to5Mac for Sleep Score bands, Apple support HT213275."

findings.topic: Backend/data architecture for a two-user, self-hosted, iPhone-only Flutter health/habit app with HealthKit ingestion

claims.claim: HealthKit gives every sample a UUID and the Flutter `health` package (v13.3.2 on pub.dev, iOS 15+, SwiftPM/CocoaPods) exposes it as HealthDataPoint.uuid, so idempotent upserts keyed on (user, uuid) are feasible. It reads workouts, sleep stages and routes.
claims.design_implication: Server table health_sample has a primary key of (user_id, hk_uuid) and ingest uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. Re-sending the same batch is harmless, so the client can retry freely.

claims.claim: The `health` package page documents no iOS background delivery, no anchored queries and no deleted-object tracking. Apple's HKAnchoredObjectQuery returns new samples plus HKDeletedObject (UUID only) against a persisted anchor, and Apple says the deletion records are temporary. Observer queries do not list deletions; pair them with an anchored query.
claims.design_implication: Plan a small custom Swift platform channel (or Flutter plugin) of roughly 200 lines. It runs HKObserverQuery with enableBackgroundDelivery and HKAnchoredObjectQuery, and stores the anchor per type. It posts upserts and tombstones to the server and advances the anchor only after the server acks. Keep the Flutter `health` package for permissions and foreground reads. This is the one place Swift is unavoidable, and it stays tiny.

claims.claim: HealthKit background delivery is advisory. Hourly is the documented cap for some types such as steps. Forum reports show wide variation, from 8-16 minutes on some devices to about 1 hour on others, and no guarantee. Health data is also unreadable while the phone is locked ('Protected health data is inaccessible').
claims.design_implication: Never depend on background push for correctness. Sync on every app foreground and on background delivery as a bonus. The server should score a day from whatever has arrived and re-score idempotently when late data lands, so scoring is a recomputable pure function of the stored data. Show the user a 'last synced' stamp.

claims.claim: Offline-first Flutter sync packages exist (syncdrift_flutter 0.1.1, sync_queue_drift 0.1.x, flutter_offline_first_sync 0.1.0) but they are all young and 0.x. Drift is the established SQLite layer.
claims.design_implication: Do not adopt a 0.x sync framework. Hand-roll a small outbox, about 150 lines, on drift: a pending_ops table of {client_op_id uuid, kind, payload, created_at}. Retry in order with exponential backoff. Every write endpoint is idempotent on client_op_id. Reads are cached in drift so screens render instantly and offline.

claims.claim: Inference: with two users and a home server that is sometimes down, the real offline need is write-capture (log a meal, tick a habit, brush teeth) and a cached read of the last-known state. Full multi-master sync is not needed, because each record has a single owner. Conflicts only arise on shared things (shared goals, challenges), which can be server-authoritative and last-write-wins.
sources: reasoning from project context; no external source
claims.design_implication: Use a hybrid: drift cache plus an outbox, with the server as the single source of truth for scores, streaks, and head-to-head. Do NOT compute streaks and points on the client. The client shows optimistic provisional values and replaces them with server values after sync.

claims.claim: Inference: Go+Postgres+Caddy and TypeScript (Hono/Next + Drizzle + Postgres) are both fine at this scale. The main differentiators are scheduled jobs and the Claude API. Both have official or supported Claude SDKs; I did not verify the current Go SDK status in this pass. Nick has shipped both stacks.
sources: reasoning from project context; Go SDK status not verified
claims.design_implication: Recommend TypeScript (Hono API + Drizzle + Postgres) with an in-process scheduler (pg-boss or node-cron) and one shared codebase with the web dashboard. The Anthropic TS SDK is the first-party default and Zod types can be shared. Choose Go if he wants a single static binary and minimal memory; this is a taste call, not a technical constraint. Before building, check the Anthropic Go SDK status via the claude-api skill.

claims.claim: Inference: SQLite would technically suffice for two users, but Postgres is already in Nick's toolbox and gives timestamptz, jsonb, generate_series for day-bucket reports, and pg-boss. The extra container is cheap on a home server.
claims.design_implication: Use Postgres. Compose with 3 services: caddy (TLS for *.npc-server.top), app (API + scheduler + web dashboard in one container), postgres with a volume plus a nightly pg_dump to another disk. Keep the scheduler in-process in the app container instead of a separate worker; split it out only if jobs block requests. Use Claude calls with claude-sonnet-4-6 per Nick's rules, in a nightly job that writes a workout plan or insight into a table, never in the request path.

claims.claim: Inference from common practice: health apps store raw per-sample rows (immutable, keyed by source UUID) and derive daily aggregates in a separate table. I did not fetch the wger, Gadgetbridge or Home Assistant schemas in this pass, so no claim is made about their internals.
sources: no verified source; wger/Gadgetbridge/HA schemas not fetched
claims.design_implication: Two layers. health_sample is the raw layer: type, value, unit, start_at and end_at as timestamptz, source, hk_uuid, tz, deleted_at. daily_metric is derived: (user_id, local_date, metric) with value, rebuilt idempotently from raw rows. Charts and scoring read daily_metric. Raw rows are kept so any metric can be recomputed when the scoring rules change.

claims.claim: Inference: 'day' must be defined in the user's local time, not UTC. Cumulative types (steps, active energy) are summed per day, while sleep belongs to the day it ends on. Travel and DST make a single fixed server timezone wrong.
claims.design_implication: Store each sample's UTC instants plus the device IANA tz at ingest time (health_sample.tz). Compute local_date = (start_at AT TIME ZONE tz)::date. Sleep: assign by end_at local date. Keep a user_tz_history table so recomputes are deterministic. Define an app-wide 'day rolls over at 04:00 local' setting for habit and meal logs, so late-night logging counts toward the same day.

claims.claim: Inference: with no real auth, pairing = enter server URL, GET /users to list the two profiles, tap your name, and POST /pair to get a random device token that is stored in the iOS Keychain. The main risks are two devices claiming one user (for example a new phone), and a stranger on the internet claiming a profile, since the domain is public.
claims.design_implication: Add a minimal gate, since the cost is small: a shared household passphrase (or a one-time 6-digit pairing code that Nick generates on the web dashboard) required at /pair. Tokens are per device (device table: id, user_id, token_hash, name, last_seen), and multiple active devices per user are allowed (new phone, iPad). Revoke is a button on the dashboard. Never rely on device HealthKit identity; it is not exposed. Alternatively keep the server on a Tailscale/LAN-only hostname and skip the passphrase.

claims.claim: Inference: a web dashboard is cheap if the API is TypeScript. Big before/after charts, year-in-review, and admin tasks (pairing codes, scoring-rule tuning, data backfill) fit better on a laptop screen than a phone.
claims.design_implication: Serve a small server-rendered or Vite/React SPA from the same container under the same domain, using Recharts or uPlot against the same JSON API. Use a Next.js app only if he wants SSR or he prefers its ergonomics; a plain Hono + static SPA is lighter. Gate by the same device-token cookie.

findings.recommended_approach:
Flutter client with drift as a read cache plus a small hand-rolled idempotent outbox. The server is authoritative for scores, streaks and head-to-head. Backend is TypeScript (Hono + Drizzle + Postgres) with an in-process pg-boss/cron scheduler. It runs daily scoring, pushes, and nightly claude-sonnet-4-6 calls, and also serves a static web dashboard, all in one app container. Compose = caddy + app + postgres, with nightly pg_dump. HealthKit ingestion is the one native piece: a thin Swift channel doing observer + anchored queries and background delivery, sending upserts keyed by (user, hk_uuid) plus tombstones from HKDeletedObject, advancing the anchor only after a server ack. Treat background delivery as best effort and sync on every foreground. Store raw samples with UTC instants and device tz, derive daily_metric by local date (sleep by end date), and make scoring a recomputable pure function.

Schema sketch:
user(id, name, tz_default)
device(id, user_id, token_hash, name, last_seen, revoked_at)
health_sample(user_id, hk_uuid PK, type, value, unit, start_at, end_at, tz, source, deleted_at)
hk_anchor(user_id, device_id, type, anchor_blob)
workout(user_id, hk_uuid PK, kind, start_at, end_at, distance_m, energy_kcal, avg_hr, tz)
daily_metric(user_id, local_date, metric, value, PK(user_id, local_date, metric))
habit_def(id, user_id, key, target_per_day, weight)
habit_log(id, client_op_id UNIQUE, user_id, habit_id, local_date, count, logged_at)
meal_log(id, client_op_id UNIQUE, user_id, local_date, name, kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, source, cooked_at_home bool)
food_item(id, barcode, name, per_100g jsonb, source)
score_event(id, user_id, local_date, rule_key, points, detail jsonb) with UNIQUE(user_id, local_date, rule_key), rebuilt idempotently
streak(user_id, habit_key, current, best, last_date)
challenge(id, kind, period, metric, handicap jsonb) and challenge_result(challenge_id, user_id, value, rank)
goal(id, user_id, year, metric, start_value, target_value)
generated_plan(id, user_id, week_start, model, prompt_hash, plan jsonb)
push_token(device_id, apns_token)
sync_op_seen(client_op_id PK, device_id, applied_at) for dedupe
alternatives: Online-only REST with optimistic UI and no local DB: simplest, but writes made while the home server is down are lost and the first screen waits on the network. Acceptable only if downtime is rare and logging is tolerant of retry.
Full local-first sync engine (PowerSync, ElectricSQL, Replicache-style): robust multi-master sync, but heavy for two users with single-owner data and adds a service to run. Not verified in this pass.
Go + Postgres + Caddy (Nick's existing pattern): equally valid, single static binary, lower memory. Cost is no shared types with a web dashboard and a separate frontend stack.
SQLite instead of Postgres in a single container with litestream backup: fewest moving parts and fine for two users; loses jsonb and generate_series conveniences.
Next.js + Drizzle full-stack (Nick's other pattern) giving API and dashboard in one framework: fine, but heavier runtime than Hono + static SPA for a mostly-JSON API.
Third-party aggregators (Vital/Junction, Spike) for HealthKit ingestion: they appeared in search results as SDKs but are cloud services, so they conflict with self-hosting; not recommended.
cannot_do: Could not verify wger, Gadgetbridge, Home Assistant or Fitbit-like schemas; the time-series modeling claim is inference from common practice (low confidence).
Could not verify the current Anthropic Go SDK status or the TS SDK version; the claude-api skill should be consulted before implementation.
Could not confirm that the `health` package lacks iOS background delivery beyond its pub.dev page, which does not document it. A pub.dev README check of its source or issue tracker is advisable.
Could not verify whether Renpho syncs to Apple Health in a way that preserves per-sample UUIDs and body composition fields. This is on the critical path for scale data.
Did not benchmark background delivery behavior on iOS 26 devices; evidence is forum reports only.
Plan mode was active, so no files were written or prototypes built.
open_questions_for_user: Is a small native Swift module for HealthKit observer/anchored queries acceptable? Without it, ingestion only happens when the app is opened.
Should the server be reachable from the public internet or only via LAN/Tailscale? This determines whether the pairing passphrase is needed.
Do you prefer TypeScript (shared code with the dashboard) or Go (single binary) for the backend?
Is a 04:00 local day rollover right for you two, or should the day end at midnight?
Do you want the web dashboard to also be an editing admin (scoring rules, handicaps) or read-only charts?
Does Renpho sync body composition into Apple Health for both of you, or will you need its own export?
How long should raw samples be kept (forever is cheap at this scale) and where should nightly backups go?

verdicts.claim: 1. HealthKit sample UUIDs are exposed by Flutter health 13.3.2 as HealthDataPoint.uuid; reads workouts, sleep stages, routes; iOS 15+, SwiftPM/CocoaPods
verdicts.evidence: pub.dev/packages/health: latest 13.3.2 (published ~2 months ago), iOS 15.0+, SwiftPM supported on Flutter 3.44+, HealthDataPoint has String uuid, getHealthDataByUUID exists, SLEEP_ASLEEP/DEEP/LIGHT/REM/SESSION types. Changelog: 11.0.0 added UUID on both platforms, 13.3.0 added WORKOUT_ROUTE.
verdicts.correction: Minor: route support is described on the page as 'writing workout routes'; the changelog says WORKOUT_ROUTE was added in 13.3.0 but I did not verify that routes can be READ on iOS (inferred, not confirmed). Also 13.3.2's headline change is write returning UUIDs.

verdicts.claim: 2. health package documents no iOS background delivery, anchored queries or deleted-object tracking; Apple anchored query returns HKDeletedObject (UUID only); deletion records temporary; observers do not list deletions
verdicts.evidence: pub.dev/packages/health and its changelog: background mentioned only for Android Health Connect (12.2.0); no anchor or deleted-object tracking mentioned. Apple doc pages (hkdeletedobject, hkanchoredobjectquery) returned only titles via the fetch tool, so Apple-side statements are from general HealthKit knowledge, not verified quotes.
verdicts.correction: The package half is verified. The 'deletion records are temporary' and 'UUID only' parts remain unverified against the Apple page text (HKDeletedObject also exposes metadata, so 'UUID only' is slightly imprecise). Design implication stands: native Swift is needed for anchored queries, and a periodic full-reconcile fallback is wise given retention uncertainty.

verdicts.claim: 3. Background delivery is advisory; hourly cap for some types; forum shows 8-16 min vs ~1 hr; protected data unreadable while locked
verdicts.evidence: developer.apple.com/forums/thread/814914: confirmed 8-16 min on three watches vs ~60 min on one (Series 10, watchOS 26.2.1), DTS says complications give ~4 updates/hr, battery >=80% matters, and that this was an App Extension on watchOS (different lifecycle). Thread 790004: docs say some types such as steps are delivered hourly; a reply (unofficial) recalls immediate/10min/hourly/daily buckets; links FB18604790. Neither thread mentions locked-device behavior or the 'Protected health data is inaccessible' string.
verdicts.correction: The variance numbers come from Apple Watch extension reports on watchOS, not iPhone apps, so they are weak evidence for an iPhone-app design. The locked-phone claim is likely true (HealthKit data protection, HKError.databaseInaccessible) but the cited threads do not support it; cite Apple's HealthKit data protection docs or drop the forum attribution. Treat background delivery as best-effort either way.

verdicts.claim: 4. Offline-first Flutter sync packages syncdrift_flutter 0.1.1, sync_queue_drift 0.1.x, flutter_offline_first_sync 0.1.0 exist, all young and 0.x; Drift is the established SQLite layer
verdicts.evidence: pub.dev: syncdrift_flutter 0.1.1 (~4 months ago), sync_queue_drift 0.1.1 (~3 months ago), flutter_offline_first_sync 0.1.1 (~30 days ago). All 0.x. Drift established status not re-fetched (known mature package).
verdicts.correction: flutter_offline_first_sync is 0.1.1, not 0.1.0. Conclusion (do not depend on them, hand-roll the outbox) unchanged.

verdicts.claim: 5. Inference: real offline need is write-capture plus cached reads; single-owner records; shared things server-authoritative LWW
verdicts.evidence: Reasoning only; no primary source applicable. Consistent with the schema (client_op_id idempotency, per-user ownership).
verdicts.correction: None needed. One caveat: head-to-head views and streaks are derived from the other person's data, so those are cached-read-only and may be stale offline; the UI should show last-synced time.

verdicts.claim: 6. Go and TypeScript both fine; both have Claude SDKs; Go SDK status unverified
verdicts.evidence: github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-go: official Go SDK, Apache-2.0, README references v2.3.0 with module path .../v2, requires Go 1.25+, ~1,006 commits, actively maintained. The README example uses model constant ModelClaudeOpus5_5.
verdicts.correction: Go SDK status is now verified: official, maintained, import path is the /v2 module. Releases page was empty in the capture, so exact release date unverified. The TS SDK was not re-checked here. Note the recommendation pins claude-sonnet-4-6; confirm that model ID is still served before hardcoding (not verified in this pass).

verdicts.claim: 7. Inference: Postgres over SQLite for jsonb, timestamptz, generate_series, pg-boss
verdicts.evidence: Reasoning only; pg-boss existence/maintenance not re-verified in this pass.
verdicts.correction: Reasonable. Verify pg-boss current major version and Postgres requirement before committing; node-cron or a simple in-process scheduler is an alternative for this scale.

verdicts.claim: 8. Inference: day must be user-local; cumulative types summed per local day; sleep belongs to the day it ends on; fixed server tz wrong
verdicts.evidence: Reasoning only; no primary source. Matches common practice for HealthKit statistics collections (day buckets computed in the device calendar).
verdicts.correction: Add: store the tz per sample (already in schema) and, for cumulative types, prefer HKStatisticsCollectionQuery on-device to avoid double-counting overlapping sources (iPhone + Watch steps); summing raw samples server-side will over-count unless de-duplicated by source priority. This is inference, not verified.

verification.revised_recommendation: The recommendation largely stands: Flutter client with Drift read cache and a hand-rolled idempotent outbox, server-authoritative scoring, thin Swift HealthKit channel with observer plus anchored queries and tombstones, foreground sync as the reliable path. Changes: (1) Keep the Dart `health` package only for convenience reads; it has no anchors or deletions on iOS, so the native Swift module owns ingestion. (2) Do not rely on the forum threads for background cadence or locked-phone behavior; they are watchOS-extension reports and do not mention locking. Handle databaseInaccessible by deferring until protected data is available, and add a periodic reconcile on foreground in case deletion records have expired. (3) For cumulative metrics (steps, active energy), use HKStatisticsCollectionQuery (or equivalent source-deduplicated aggregation) rather than summing raw samples, to avoid iPhone/Watch double counting. (4) Go is a viable alternative: the official anthropic-sdk-go v2 is maintained (Go 1.25+), so the TS choice should rest on Nick's preference and scheduler ergonomics, not SDK availability. (5) Verify pg-boss version and the pinned Claude model ID before implementation. Correct the flutter_offline_first_sync version to 0.1.1."

missing_features_or_flows: First-run onboarding and pairing flow: server address entry, who-am-I selection, the per-person data checklist (equipment, schedule, targets, injuries, meds), HealthKit permission walkthrough. Only fragments exist (architecture device/token_hash, passphrase question); no topic owns the screen flow, re-pairing after reinstall, or a lost phone.
To-do list with task-completion rewards is not covered by any topic. No schema table (architecture has habit_log but no todo/task), no scoring weight in gamification, no notifications design for it.

Reward for not ordering food out / DoorDash is only a nutrition weight line. Nothing says how it is detected (self-report? bank/email receipts? 'cooked at home' toggle), how the honor system is verified, or what counts on days with no dinner logged.

Year-long goal and start-vs-now metrics: architecture has a goal table, but no topic defines which metrics, baseline capture at day 1 (weight, 1-mile time, pushups max, resting HR, VO2max), how Jan-to-Dec progress is displayed, or what the year-end reward is.
Math problems as a standalone feature: only appears as the alarm dismissal check. No design for daily math practice, difficulty, scoring, or whether it is a habit at all.

Pushups / pull-ups / miles head-to-head: HealthKit gives workouts and distance but not rep counts. No topic defines manual rep logging, a strength-test or max-reps challenge flow, or how Hall of Fame raw totals are captured.

Workout logging UX during a session: sets, reps, weights, rest timer, Watch companion or not. The generator is covered but the in-session logger, exercise swap UI and history/progression view are not.

Meal planning loop that actually drives 'cook more at home': recipe selection, weekly meal plan, shopping list, pantry, and the daily 'what's for dinner' nudge. Nutrition covers Mealie as an option but no topic ties it to scoring (cooked_at_home flag) or to the 5pm nag.

Calorie and macro targets: no topic computes TDEE/goal calories or protein targets from weight and body goals, and gamification deliberately avoids calorie scoring, so the purpose of calorie tracking is undefined.

Running-specific flow: run tracking source (Watch workout import only vs in-app), plan display, treadmill runs (no GPS, distance from Watch), and Watch-side delivery of the plan. WorkoutKit was unverified.
Weekly and monthly recap / review screen and the LLM narrative. Mentioned as a notification and a job but with no screen or data design.

Settings and admin: editing targets, availability weekly check-in, rest days, scoring weights, partner-flag/dispute resolution UI, data correction. Gamification assumes these exist; architecture only offers a maybe-admin web dashboard.
Failure and offline modes beyond sync: home server down, domain/cert expiry, how a TestFlight build behaves with no backend, and backup restore for Postgres.

Home server exposure and reachability: *.npc-server.top domain, Caddy TLS, LAN-only vs public vs Tailscale. Notifications topic needs APNs outbound from the server, and phones need to reach it away from home.
Watch app: nobody decided if there is a watchOS app. Several features (one-tap creatine, workout start, quick teeth tap, plan on wrist) imply one, and it changes signing and build.
Screen-time 'not typing password / ignoring limit' incentive from the original note has no workable source (explicitly cannot detect). No replacement mechanic is proposed.
Sleep and wake: wake-up improvement beyond alarm - e.g. wind-down routine, caffeine cutoff, light exposure - and the 'Huel in the morning' sequence tied to wake time are not connected.
Data export, year-end archive, and what happens to data if the relationship or the app stops (low priority but missing). Also onboarding of a future third person is explicitly out of scope; confirm.
Tracking of reading as 'instead of videos': no mechanism to measure video time (YouTube etc.), only screen-time buckets or Shortcuts open counts.
risky_assumptions: Background HealthKit sync via a custom Swift shim is treated as a core design element in healthkit and architecture topics, yet delivery is best-effort, evidence is only watchOS reports, and iPhone iOS 26 behavior is untested. Daily scoring, streaks and the head-to-head depend on data arriving; the partner's view will often be stale or missing mid-day.

Apple Watch worn to bed by both, every night, is assumed by the sleep model (and HRV, workout, HR-zone effort points). If Nadia charges overnight or Nick forgets, sleep scoring, effort-based workout points and readiness all degrade. Neutral-skip rules cover only 1 night per week.

suggested_mvp_cut: Week-one foundation: Flutter app, Go (or TS, pick one) + Postgres + Caddy in Docker Compose behind a *.npc-server.top host, pick-your-name pairing with a device token, onboarding checklist that captures targets, schedule and equipment, TestFlight internal build via CI with the 90-day rebuild scheduled and alerted.

Habit core with immediate reward: daily check-ins for teeth AM/PM, creatine, Huel, no-eating-out and home-cooked dinner, using local repeating notifications with Done actions and a home-screen streak widget (or in-app only if the widget extension is too costly). Duolingo-style streaks with rest days and freezes, one simple forgiveness rule.

HealthKit read on app open only (no background delivery in v1): steps, workouts, distance, weight/body fat from Renpho, resting HR, sleep duration. Use the `health` package, no Swift shim yet, plus a 'last synced' indicator. Capture day-1 baseline metrics for the year start-vs-now page.

Simple, transparent scoring: personal targets set by hand at onboarding (no median/capacity engine yet), daily points over 5 to 6 habits with one cap, weekly shared quest plus a light weekly duel as percent of own target, and a household streak. Hall of Fame tab with manual pushup and mile totals.
Fairness in v1 is a manual weekly availability toggle (normal, busy, horse day) that scales that person's targets, shown to both. Defer calendar integration and capacity math.

Cooking at home loop: manual meal log with 'cooked at home' flag, quick-add calories and protein, favorites and recents, and a single USDA/OFF barcode lookup with a manual-entry fallback. Defer LLM label scanning, Mealie and the preloaded Branded import.
